Section: Professorinnen und Professoren Prof. Dr.-Ing. Heiko Zatocil Aktives Netzfilters zur Kompensation von Stromharmonischen

# Aktives Netzfilters zur Kompensation von Stromharmonischen

#### Regelung eines aktiven Netzfilters zur Kompensation von Stromoberschwingungen nichtlinearer Lasten und zur Reduktion der Netzanschlussleistung.

####

#### Projektziel

In zahlreichen industriellen Anwendungen werden Verbraucher über ungesteuerte Diodenbrücken aus dem dreiphasigen Netz gespeist. Diese nichtlinearen Lasten entnehmen dem Netz einen pulsförmigen, stark oberschwingungsbehafteten Strom. Die Oberschwingungsströme führen zu Leistungsanteilen, die zwischen Netz und Last hin- und herpendeln, ohne nennenswert zur Energieübertragung beizutragen. Dennoch müssen Netzanschluss, Leitungen und Absicherung auf den dadurch erhöhten Effektivwert des Netzstroms und die entsprechend größere Scheinleistung ausgelegt werden.

Ein aktiver Netzfilter, ausgeführt als Pulswechslrichter, bietet die Möglichkeit diese Oberschwingungen gezielt zu kompensieren. Parallel zur Last angeschlossen, prägt er die unerwünschten Anteile des Laststroms gegenphasig ein, sodass das Netz idealerweise nur noch den sinusförmigen Grundschwingungsstrom liefern muss. Auf diese Weise lässt sich die erforderliche Netzanschlussleistung der Anwendung reduzieren, ohne die Last selbst zu verändern.

Im Rahmen des Projekts soll daher eine Regelungsstruktur für den aktiven Netzfilter entwickelt werden, die eine dynamische Stromregelung zur selektiven Kompensation der Oberschwingungen mit einer überlagerten Zwischenkreisregelung verbindet.

#### Projektlaufzeit

Juli 2026 bis September 2027

title: Cybersecurity zwischen Forschung und Praxis
content:
Cybersecurity zwischen Forschung und Praxis
Section: Hochschule Fakultäten Fakultät EMI

# Cybersecurity zwischen Forschung und Praxis

Ob Unternehmen, öffentliche Einrichtungen oder Privatpersonen – Cyberkriminalität betrifft längst alle Bereiche des gesellschaftlichen Lebens. Wie sich digitale Bedrohungen entwickeln und welche Risiken damit verbunden sind, stand im Mittelpunkt der Open Innovation Night am Dienstagabend.

Organisiert wurde die Veranstaltung in Kooperation zwischen der Wirtschaftsförderung Amberg, der IHK-Geschäftsstelle Amberg-Sulzbach und der Fakultät Elektrotechnik, Medien und Informatik der OTH Amberg-Weiden. Alexander Seitz von der Wirtschaftsförderung Amberg und Prof. Dr. Ulrich Schäfer, Dekan der Fakultät, begrüßten die 65 Gäste und führten gemeinsam durch das Programm.

### Von gesetzlichen Vorgaben bis zur Cyberkriminalität vor Ort

Den fachlichen Auftakt gestaltete Prof. Dr. Christian Roth mit einem Vortrag zum Cyber Resilience Act. Er erläuterte, welche Anforderungen die europäische Verordnung an Hersteller digitaler Produkte stellt und welche Pflichten zur Dokumentation, Offenlegung und Meldung von Sicherheitslücken damit verbunden sind.

Anschließend zeigte Kriminalhauptkommissar Patrick Preiß, wie sich Cyberkriminalität verändert und welche Auswirkungen neue Bedrohungen auf Staat, Wirtschaft und Gesellschaft haben. Anhand konkreter Fälle aus seinem Berufsalltag, darunter auch Beispiele aus der Region, verdeutlichte er, dass Cyberangriffe keine abstrakte Gefahr sind, sondern längst zum Alltag der Ermittlungsbehörden gehören.

### Wenn das eigene Gesicht und die eigene Stimme zur Täuschung werden

Wie einfach sich mithilfe Künstlicher Intelligenz digitale Identitäten manipulieren lassen, demonstrierte David Trott von der Fakultät Elektrotechnik, Medien und Informatik. In einer Live-Vorführung wurden die Gesichter von Besuchern in einen fingierten Videoanruf eingebunden und mithilfe von Deepfake-Technologie in Echtzeit ausgetauscht.

Auch die Stimmen der Gäste wurden zum Gegenstand der Demonstration: Innerhalb weniger Sekunden analysierte eine KI die Stimmen der Besucher und imitierte sie. Dies zeigte eindrucksvoll, welches Missbrauchspotenzial in modernen Sprachmodellen steckt. Die Vorführung machte anschaulich, wie sich bekannte Betrugsmaschen wie der Enkeltrick durch täuschend echte Stimmen und Videobilder zu einem „Enkeltrick 2.0“ weiterentwickeln können.

### Live-Hacking: Wenn manipulierte Daten zur Gefahr werden

Dass Cyberangriffe nicht nur digitale Daten, sondern auch reale Anlagen und Menschen gefährden können, zeigte Maximilian Wilke vom Unternehmen BxC. Am Beispiel einer Methanolproduktionsanlage demonstrierte er live, wie Angreifer durch die Manipulation von Sensorwerten in industrielle Prozesse eingreifen können.

Die Vorführung verdeutlichte, welche weitreichenden Folgen vermeintlich kleine Eingriffe in digitale Steuerungssysteme haben können. Werden sicherheitsrelevante Messwerte gezielt verfälscht, können daraus erhebliche Risiken für den Anlagenbetrieb und die beteiligten Menschen entstehen.

### Digitale Sicherheit gemeinsam stärken

Die Open Innovation Night verband wissenschaftliche Erkenntnisse mit Erfahrungen aus der Polizeiarbeit und anschaulichen technischen Demonstrationen. Die 65 Gäste erhielten damit nicht nur Einblicke in aktuelle Angriffsmethoden, sondern auch ein besseres Verständnis dafür, warum digitale Sicherheit Unternehmen, Institutionen und Privatpersonen gleichermaßen fordert.

Die Veranstaltung zeigte zugleich den Wert des Austauschs zwischen Hochschule, Wirtschaft und Sicherheitsbehörden. Denn um den zunehmend komplexen Bedrohungen zu begegnen, braucht es neben technischen Schutzmaßnahmen vor allem Wissen, Aufmerksamkeit und ein gemeinsames Bewusstsein für digitale Risiken.

# Ostbayerische Technische Hochschule Amberg-Weiden

Welcome to the OTH Amberg-Weiden!
Practical, innovative, sustainable and future-oriented - in study, teaching, research and transfer. 1

## About the Ostbayerische Technische Hochschule Amberg-Weiden (OTH)

The Ostbayerische Technische Hochschule Amberg-Weiden (technical university of applied sciences) is located in the Upper Palatinate, an administrative district of the federal state of Bavaria. It is home to four departments on two campuses in Amberg and Weiden, respectively, about 40 kilometers apart.

With approximately 4,000 students the University offers excellent conditions and career prospects. In addition to the regular academic programmes, students can choose from a variety of extra-curricular courses and activities to sharpen their skills and broaden their minds. Our graduates are in great demand on the regional and national labour markets, and our University constantly secures top places in university rankings.

Our main objective has been and still is to provide our students with a practical, theory-based education in close cooperation with our partners from business and industry. This practical orientation draws much of its strength from our professors’ extensive hands-on experience – all of them have worked outside academia for at least five years. Students benefit from small group teaching, practical seminars and laboratories and a compulsory work placement.

## OTH Amberg-Weiden: Study@ItsBest

Feel at home, benefit from an excellent study environment and pay no tuition fees.

Ostbayerische Technische Hochschule Amberg-Weiden (OTH AW) is a young, up-and-coming, innovative University of Applied Sciences in the heart of Eastern Bavaria. With our campuses in Amberg (departments of mechanical and environmental engineering, information and media technology) and Weiden (departments of business, industrial engineering and health), about 40 kilometers apart, we provide first-class higher education in a region outside the major urban centers. Due to our excellent study facilities, a large bandwidth of Bachelor and Master programs in German as well as English, and close ties with the industry, our highly trained graduates strengthen the businesses in the region and beyond. Our study programs cover current topics such as Artificial Intelligence, Digital Business, Medical Technology, Management and Sustainability and International Business. University rankings prove that we do a good job: we regularly finish at the top of the competition.
We look forward to welcoming you to OTH Amberg-Weiden! international@oth-aw.de

## You are looking for future-oriented study programs?

OTH Amberg-Weiden combines cutting-edge study programs with the feel@home atmosphere reserved for small, exquisite schools.

Choose from a number of bachelor programs such as Artificial Intelligence, Digital Business, Medical Technology, Geoinformatics & Land Management, Motorsport Engineering, Media Technology & Production, or Energy Efficiency, to name a few.

Earn a second-level degree in one of our consecutive master programs, for example in Applied Research in Engineering Sciences, Information Technology & Automation, Digital Entrepreneurship, Environmental Technology or Intercultural Business & Technology Management.

Boost your career by benefiting from our close ties to industry partners, extra-curricular courses, excursions, and company visits.

Enjoy our extra-curricular activities, university sports programmes and excursions as well as the vibrant campus life.

## What we offer…

- Over 30 bachelor programs, some of which – like Digital Technology Management – are taught in English;
- Over 20 master programs, some of which – e.g. Artificial Intelligence for Industrial Applications – are taught in English;
- A very good student-professor-ratio – our professors know their students personally and encourage them to maximize their career opportunities;
- Perfect student support through administrative facilities, such as the International Office, the Student Affairs Office, the Center for Gender and Diversity, the Language Center, the 24-Hour Library, the Council of Student Representation and our Industry Network;

## Why Amberg-Weiden?

- Both campuses are equipped with top standard facilities in a personal and safe environment and each is situated in a beautiful historic town.
- Our state-of-the-art laboratories enable you to gain first-hand experience with new technologies.
- Both locations can be considered as very safe and the well-being of our university family has top priority.
- The cost of living in Amberg and Weiden is affordable compared to the bigger cities in Germany.
- We host newly built and furnished student accommodation (single apartments) – they’re in great demand, make sure you register well in advance.
- Amberg and Weiden both offer a wide array of cultural events, and they are surrounded by beautiful nature, giving you the peace to concentrate on your studies when you need it. The Bavarian cities Munich, Regensburg and Nuremberg are all in short distance.
- Many of our professors and researchers come from companies and industries close by and therefore bring a wealth of practical expertise to the classroom.

Get in touch. We look forward to welcoming you to OTH Amberg-Weiden!

Contact us at: international@oth-aw.de

# Evaluation

[Image: Evaluation control loop of OTH Amberg-Weiden]

Internal and external evaluations serve the purposes of quality assurance and quality improvement. They are therefore a central element of OTH Amberg-Weiden's quality management system. Regular feedback from students, lecturers, graduates and external assessors enables the university to critically evaluate its academic programmes, counseling services and support offerings from various perspectives and, when necessary, to initiate appropriate measures to improve the quality of teaching and learning along with the study conditions.

### Course Evaluation

Students regularly provide feedback to lecturers on their attended courses. These evaluations are conducted at faculty level. The results form the basis for a joint discussion between lecturers and students. They highlight areas for potential improvement and are incorporated into the teaching review meeting which takes place regularly between faculty and university management.

### First-year Student Survey

The initial phase of a degree programme plays a crucial role in the student’s subsequent academic journey. With the aim of systematically improving its services, OTH Amberg-Weiden regularly surveys first-year students about their start to university life. Key topics include perceptions of OTH Amberg-Weiden, the decision to study there, settling in at the university and an assessment of the guidance and support services available at the start of their degree programme.

### Bachelor's Survey

In order to assess the quality of current academic conditions from the students’ perspective, OTH Amberg-Weiden regularly surveys its Bachelor’s students. The survey focuses on the course content, the curriculum and the level of support provided within each degree programme. In addition, students assess their workload, their examination experience and the general conditions of studying at the university. This feedback enables OTH Amberg-Weiden to identify strengths and areas for improvement in its degree programmes and, where necessary, to initiate appropriate measures.

### Master's Survey

OTH Amberg-Weiden regularly surveys students on its consecutive and professional Master’s programmes about their study experience. The survey focuses on the transition from a Bachelor’s to a Master’s degree and an assessment of the respective programme, including workload, examination conditions and general study conditions. Students on professional Master’s programmes are also asked additional questions about their specific study and supervision arrangements.

### Graduate Survey

OTH Amberg-Weiden currently takes part in the Bavarian Graduate Survey (BAS) (https://www.bap.ihf.bayern.de/en/bas/background) every year. This survey is conducted externally by the Bavarian State Institute for Higher Education Research and Planning (IHF) in Munich and is aimed at Bachelor’s and Master’s graduates approximately 1.5 years after their graduation. The survey focuses on a retrospective assessment of the quality of the degree programme, an evaluation of the skills acquired and their career start or rather their transition to a further degree programme.

### Event-related Survey

#### Digital Teaching Survey

The COVID-19 pandemic presented all members of the university community with a major challenge that was both unforeseeable and sudden. Teaching was almost entirely moved online. But were all those involved sufficiently prepared (technically) for such a far-reaching change? Did distance learning work? What advantages and disadvantages did the digital learning environment bring for teaching and studying? To find this out, all students and teaching staff were invited on several occasions during the pandemic to take part in a survey conducted by the Research and Innovation Laboratory for Digital Teaching (FIDL).

### Internal Assessment

#### Teaching Review Meeting

The teaching review meeting takes place in each faculty at least once every three years. The aim of the meeting between representatives of the university management and the faculties is to discuss quality-related aspects of the degree programmes as well as potential areas for improvement in the organisation and structure of the programmes. Student representatives are involved in a public session held at the start of the meeting.

### External Assessment

#### Beiräte und Peers

External experts are regularly invited to critically review and monitor the individual degree programmes. Aim of the external review is to obtain recommendations from independent experts on the introduction and further development of OTH Amberg-Weiden's degree programmes. Whilst a group of advisory board members regularly reviews the academic and content-related aspects of the degree programmes, individual peers assess the quality-related criteria on an ad hoc basis as required (e.g. prior to the introduction of degree programmes). Professors from other universities specialising in related fields qualify as peers; members of the advisory board also include company representatives, external students and alumni. An advisory board meeting takes place at least once every two calendar years.

title: News / Events
content:
News / Events

## News / Events

## Hóla - Ciao - Hello! Save your spot in Amberg!

## Final examination English UNIcert III for Professional Purposes in WEIDEN

The final examination of the language course English UNIcert III for Professional Purposes in Weiden

will take place on July 23rd 2026 in Weiden, 08.00, WIG 139.

We wish you every success!

## The language centre wishes you best of luck with your exams!

The language centre kicked off the exam period last week: all German and English exams in Amberg took place on Friday. Afterwards it was finally time to say ‘Hoch die Hände, Wochenende!’

The whole team wishes all students good luck (and perhaps a bit of fun too) with their upcoming exams!

## Dobrá práce! Students get Unicert® Basis Czech certificates

“Why wander far away when good things are so close?” If you want to learn an exciting new language, you don't have to travel far. So why not learn Czech and discover our neighbouring country on a whole new level? Just like the graduates of our Unicert® Basic Czech course, who can now celebrate their foreign language certificate after two semesters. Well done! Dobrá práce!

## Have a relaxing semester break!

The Language Centre team wishes you all a nice and relaxing semester break!

See you soon!

## Students delighted with Unicert® III certificates

2025

Zertifikatsübergabe 2025

Zertifikatsübergabe 2024

11.12.2024

The participants of the UNIcert ® III English course were finally handed over their language certificate - a valuable document that not only demonstrates language competence, but also the ability to communicate interculturally. Moreover it is a confirmation of the students' hard work and commitment.

Since 2001, the Language Centre has been running language courses from the UNIcert ® language programme - a nationally recognised, practice-oriented and demanding training and examination system offered exclusively at universities.

Congratulations to all graduates and well done!

## Our English UNIcert II courses have been restructured: Get the UNIcert certificate in only 2 semesters!

With the start of the semester, our UNIcert II courses only consist of two modules, which we offer alternately at each of our locations:

Business English in Weiden: Mondays, 15.45 - 19.00 (4 SWS/5 ECTS), starts on 24 March 2025, room WTC 1.29

Technical English in Amberg: Thursdays, 15.30 - 18.45 (4 SWS/5 ECTS), starts on 20 March 2025, room MBUT 024

Register here!

## BintHo-Report: Positive feedback for German courses

A reason to celebrate! According to a Germany-wide survey conducted as part of the DAAD's ‘Benchmark internationale Hochschule’ (BintHo) project, international students at OTH Amberg-Weiden rate the quality German courses at our Language Centre above average.

Compared to other universities of applied sciences, not only do more students take advantage of the German courses on offer, they also feel better supported in developing their language skills. This is mostly the merit of our German lecturers, a big thank you for that!

You snooze, you lose: Our German course programme is constantly being expanded. You will find information about upcoming courses on our website from February on!

## New: German-English glossary for university context

For German-English translations for a university context you can now look up the most important administrative terms used at our university under the "Glossary" menu item on the Language Centre website.

There you will also find links to external glossaries or translation guidelines.

## UNIcert certificates are ready to pick up at the Language Centre!

As of now, UNIcert certificates for Russian and English can be picked up at the Language Centre in Weiden, room WTC 1.32.

## 20 years UNIcert® at the OTH Amberg-Weiden

20 years ago, in the summer semester of 2002, the first language courses from the UNIcert® language program started at OTH Amberg-Weiden.

Today, we can draw a thoroughly positive balance: Since the summer semester of 2002, a total of 6272 students have taken part in the courses at OTH Amberg-Weiden and 1298 UNIcert® certificates have already been issued for the languages English, Polish, Russian and Czech. Our students benefit from a clearly structured course program with courses that build on each other and acquire a meaningful certificate that transparently documents and attests to the skills they have acquired. The multilingual certificate is recognized by German and, in some cases, foreign universities as proof, e.g. when applying for a place on a master's program, and is a plus point for application documents.

Also in the Corona semester, various language courses from the UNIcert® language program were offered and in the summer semester 2021, a total of 29 students completed their language training with a UNIcert® certificate - congratulations!

# Financing / BAFöG

## Student financing

Unfortunately, studying is not free. Travel costs, rent and food, learning materials and books, clothing, health insurance, mobile phone and internet costs...

The financing is often taken over by the parents and many students earn extra money by working. Other ways to afford your studies are:

## BAföG and KfW Student Loan

According to the Federal Training Assistance Act (Bundesausbildungsförderungsgesetz, BAföG), German students and, under certain conditions, foreign students can receive financial assistance if they are unable to finance their studies on their own or with the help of persons liable to pay maintenance. You can find information about BAföG at the Studentenwerk Oberfranken (http://www.studentenwerk-oberfranken.de/) .

The KfW Student Loan can also be used to finance living expenses during a course of study. You can find more information at the KfW (https://www.kfw.de/inlandsfoerderung/Privatpersonen/Studieren-Qualifizieren/Studium-finanzieren/?kfwmc=vt.sea.google.{Kampagne}.{Anzeigengruppe}.{Anzeige}&wt_cc1=bildung&wt_cc2=pri|studieren-qualifizieren&wt_cc3=82025713368_kwd-3380680344_620544759097&wt_kw=p_82025713368_studienkredit%20kfw) .

## Stipendien

Incidentally, it is not only the "highly gifted" who can get a scholarship. In addition to good grades at school or university, many foundations take into account voluntary work or personal circumstances.

State-funded foundations
There are a number of foundations for the promotion of gifted students that provide financial and non-material support for students. Most of these foundations pursue a specific goal and, in addition to good school or study performance, place value on voluntary work or address a specific target group, such as persons with a migration background or first-year students who have completed vocational training.
You can find a list of these foundations at Stipendium Plus (http://www.stipendiumplus.de/startseite.html) .

Special funding programmes
We would like to draw special attention to the following funding programmes, as they have a local or subject-related connection for students at OTH Amberg-Weiden or take into account the special nature of an existing vocational training programme

- Deutschlandstipendium
- Otto-Carl-Schulz-Stiftung der DEPRAG SCHULZ GmbH & Co. KG (https://www.deprag.com/de/unternehmen/wir-ueber-uns/engagement.html)
- Max-Weber-Programm des Freistaats Bayern (https://www.elitenetzwerk.bayern.de/start/foerderangebote/max-weber-programm)
- Oskar-Karl-Forster-Stipendium
Students in need at state universities, universities of applied sciences and art colleges in Bavaria can apply for a one-off grant to purchase books or other learning materials. Application is made to the Studien- und Career Service
- Aufstiegsstipendium (https://www.sbb-stipendien.de/aufstiegsstipendium.html)

## Deutschlandstipendium

Half of this scholarship is funded by the BMBF and half by sponsors (companies, associations, private individuals). More information on the Deutschlandstipendium .

# School visits

[Image: Informationsvortrag im neuen Hörsaalgebäude in Weiden]

### Presentations

The team of the Study and Career Service will be happy to come to your class and inform you about the study programmes offered by OTH Amberg-Weiden. If you wish, we can also be accompanied by students who report on their everyday study life.

### Become a cooperation school?

We have a close partnership with our cooperation schools. In addition to the exchange of information, the focus is on technical projects. In this way, the students should gain their first experience of OTH Amberg-Weiden and of specialist topics in the fields of technology and business.

The schools are important partners for us in order to make it easier for the students to make the transition to university. The close cooperation with some schools has already resulted in a cooperation agreement. Within the framework of such a "privileged partnership", the schools work on projects with the university. The advantage: in this way, the pupils get to grips with research topics at an early stage. They are familiarised with university studies, the choice of subject is actively supported and inhibitions about academic training are reduced.

title: "Praxistage" 2027
content:
"Praxistage" 2027
Section: University About our university Facilities

# "Praxistage" 2027

### Your Springboard to the Future

The next “Praxistage” will take place from March 1 to 12, 2027 . During this time, you can visit regional companies, gain insights into projects and work processes, and discover what career opportunities are available to you after you graduate.

What are the “Praxistage”?

The “Praxistage” are one of the largest career events for students in Bavaria. Over the course of ten days, around 200 companies and organizations across Bavaria open their doors and offer a glimpse “behind the scenes.” At the approximately 300 events , you’ll have the opportunity to get a taste of what it’s like and discover potential career paths.

A diverse range of employers from a wide variety of industries will participate. These include well-known names, as well as many social organizations and “hidden champions.” The exact list of participants will be published at the end of the year .

No elaborate application process is required—all you need to do is register briefly at jobboerse.oth-aw.de/praxistage (https://jobboerse.oth-aw.de/en/praxistage) (starting in January 2027 ). Whether it’s an exciting plant tour, a Scrum workshop, a casual lunch with the executives, a visit to a major construction site, or experiencing the day-to-day work at a social organization — each company has put together its own customized program.

The “Praxistage” are explicitly not just for graduates ! Students can also take advantage of the “Praxistage” early in their studies to set the course for internships, their thesis, or a part-time student job . This is where doors to your professional future open!

More information (https://jobboerse.oth-aw.de/en/praxistage)

## FAQ

When and where are the films shown?
Films are (almost) always shown on Wednesdays at 7:30 PM.
This semester, we’ve had to move to Lecture Hall 301 in the EMI building as an exception. From next semester on, we’ll be back in the Audimax ;)
Doors open at 7:00 PM. The film starts at 7:30 PM.

Who is the student cinema for?
Within the framework of our licenses, lecture hall cinemas should not compete with commercial cinemas, and we don't want to do that anyway. Therefore, the cinema evenings and our advertising are fundamentally directed only internally to university members/affiliates (students and staff of universities). However, members of other universities are also allowed to attend. In addition, visitors may be accompanied by people from their closest personal circle (e.g. friends, life partners, children), even if they are not university members.

What about the "club fee"?
We show films. But we're not the only ones doing that ;-) However, for our prices to remain student-friendly, our screenings must not be public. For this reason, we are a film club with a (more or less) small circle of student film enthusiasts.

What's the deal with the app?
The app is not an invention or development of ours, but is used by all student cinemas of the entire unifilm network and has to do with the licensing restrictions that we are also subject to. It replaces the previously used paper club cards and is therefore mandatory for all visitors.

What films are shown?
Films that are available on DVD/Blu-Ray (as current as possible). We CANNOT show current cinema films, as we would otherwise be in competition with local cinema operators. Besides, we wouldn't get a license for that either...

I have another question...
No problem. Simply send an email to cinerama@unifilm.de or ask someone from the Cinerama team next Monday…

## Screening of the documentary film ‘Running Towards New Horizons’

02.11.2026
Electrical Engineering, Media and Computer Science

Concerns/Category:

- All courses
- All around studies
- Events/University sports

Dokumentarfilms „Running Towards New Horizons“

Dear students, dear colleagues,

Imagine running around 170 kilometres non-stop. Not on the road, but along mountain trails, through forests and over mountain passes, with an elevation gain of around 10,000 metres, through the night and without a break. That is trail running in its most extreme form. And that is precisely what the UTMB around Mont Blanc is – the most famous race in this sport.

In 2024, a runner from Ecuador finished third there, becoming the first Latin American ever to reach the podium. His name is Joaquín López. Most of you have probably never heard of him.

For my Master’s thesis, I followed him for a year to find out how someone gets that far. The answer surprised me: there was no miracle and no talent that fell from the sky. There was simply a person who started at some point and never stopped. “Running Towards New Horizons” is a film for anyone who sometimes doubts themselves. Filmed in Ecuador and Spain, produced in Japan and Germany.

📅 Thursday, 5 November 2026, 11.00 am to 12.10 pm

📍 Room 211, EMI Faculty, OTH Amberg-Weiden, Amberg campus

11.00 am: Film (36 mins, original English version)

11.36 am: Behind the scenes

11.45 am: Q&A and discussion

Do come along, bring your friends – I look forward to seeing you!

Best regards,

Sebastián Ortiz

BARMER is inviting international students to a free online workshop entitled ‘Survival Guide Germany’. The workshop will be conducted in English and is specifically tailored to the needs of first-year international students. The format has been successfully established at numerous colleges and universities in Bavaria for many years and is regularly used as a supplementary information resource as part of preparatory studies. The focus is on providing impartial information on the organisational steps to take before and after arriving in Germany.

During the workshop, which lasts around 60 minutes, information will be provided on, amongst other things::

- the compulsory health insurance for students in Germany,,
- options for exemption from the compulsory insurance,
- differences between statutory and private health insurance,
- important steps to take before arrival,
- organisational requirements after arrival,
- useful points of contact and sources of information to ensure a successful start to your studies.

Naturally, the workshop will also provide information on the procedure for exemption from compulsory health insurance, as well as an impartial overview of the options available between statutory and private health insurance, so that you can make a well-founded and informed decision.

The aim is to provide guidance before arrival, allay any uncertainties and help avoid typical mistakes when preparing to study in Germany. At the same time, the aim is to support universities in enabling their international students to get off to a successful start in Germany.

As the semester begins, here’s a quick reminder about using the revolving door and the 24-hour library:

All students can gain 24-hour access by attending a one-time library orientation session. The revolving door is also explained during this session.

We continue to offer sessions for this; please feel free to stop by the library or check our website for details.

We strongly ask that you follow our rules:

Use your own student ID card to operate the revolving door!

Go through the revolving door one at a time!

Take your time! The door takes a few seconds to open.

Do not force the revolving door to turn any further!!! It rotates completely automatically.

If it does not turn, your access is likely not active. Please feel free to ask us at the service desk—we’ll be happy to help.

Only if all students follow these rules can we continue to offer the 24-hour library.

If multiple people enter the revolving door at the same time or if people force their way in, the mechanism will break. Please follow the rules so that everyone can use the 24-hour library.

How can you tell if you have access to the revolving door? The card reader will light up blue around the edge.

If you do not have access, the card reader will light up red.

Take advantage of our current training sessions and get access for the rest of your studies!

Thank you very much for your understanding and cooperation!

## New semester, new library system, new OPAC!

Library

Concerns/Category:

- All courses

You may have already noticed: the OTH Library recently implemented a new management system and a new OPAC/library catalog.

This also means a few changes for you, our users:

-
students will receive all emails from the library exclusively at their OTH email address. Please check your inbox regularly!

-
With the new, more modern OPAC ( https://katalog.oth-aw.de (https://katalog.oth-aw.de/) ), the login process has also changed: students must now log in using their university ID and the corresponding password.

-
Longer loan periods—automatic renewals are now available: in addition to the standard 4-week loan period, borrowed books are automatically renewed 5 times, each time for four weeks.
If there are no holds on the items, students can therefore keep borrowed books for up to 6 months.
Please check your OPAC account or OTH email inbox regularly: when the loan period expires and you need to return the books, you’ll receive a reminder email!
(You can no longer renew items yourself via the OPAC. If you’re eligible for a renewal, it will happen automatically.)

- Change to the interlibrary loan service for copies: With the system change, the direct download link that was previously included in the email notification is no longer available.
You can now download the materials via your interlibrary loan account, which you can access after logging into OPAC by going to Account -> Orders -> Interlibrary Loan Orders ( https://katalog.oth-aw.de/vufind/Holds/List (https://katalog.oth-aw.de/vufind/Holds/List) ).

Any other questions? No problem! Just send us an email at bib@oth-aw.de or ask at the library counter—we’re happy to help!

We’re looking forward to offering you even better, more efficient, and more enjoyable service with our new library system in the future!

The course will be updated in the module handbook soon.

We also offer Advanced courses from vhb as online options for those who can't come to campus every week.

You can find a list of the accepted Advanced courses in the module handbook on p.31.

In the timetable you can find out whether the courses will be held weekly, or as a block course at the weekend, or online (use the search function as these courses appear on separate pages in the timetable).

vhb courses are not listed in the timetable. Information on the procedure as well as exam dates of vhb courses can be found in the respective course description at vhb.

According to the new process of crediting, you have to register for vhb exams at the vhb and at OTH via Primuss.

After you have passed the exam at vhb and received your certificate, you can hand in your certificate and the course will be credited automatically.

# Campus Amberg in Detail

Address:

92224 Amberg

Directions (https://www.google.com/maps/dir//Kaiser-Wilhelm-Ring+23,+92224+Amberg/@49.4440917,11.8465784,17z/data=!4m9!4m8!1m0!1m5!1m1!1s0x47a02a48553b3e35:0x9d4db07d0427cf90!2m2!1d11.8488261!2d49.4435476!3e2)

Download Lageplan als PDF (https://www.oth-aw.de/files/oth-aw/Standorte/Lageplan_OTH-AW_Amberg.pdf)

Adresse:

92224 Amberg

## Why to study in Amberg?

Amberg is not a metropolis of millions like Berlin, Hamburg or Munich. So why study here? Quite simply because it all comes down to the overall package.

We provide you with teaching of excellent quality. With about 1,500 students at the Amberg location, you will enjoy very good study conditions. Our university offers excellent support from our professors, lecturers and staff, as well as short and uncomplicated communication channels.

Our location in Amberg offers everything a campus needs so that you, as a student, can learn, develop creatively and conduct research. The architecture of the former Kaiser Wilhelm barracks not only provides space for lectures, seminars and group work. It also impresses with modern laboratories, excellent IT infrastructure, a well-equipped library and a cozy cafeteria. Between your events, the idyllic inner courtyard invites you to relax among trees, lawns and art.

The campus's direct connection to Amberg's city center allows you to get to cafés, shopping arcades and most cultural attractions without having to drive or take the bus. Irrespective of this, public transport connections in Amberg are very well developed.

Just as important as a functioning transportation infrastructure for Amberg is the expansion of the broadband network. Therefore, access to high-performance Internet exists for every resident in Amberg, which is especially indispensable for students.

Living in Amberg is nice and, above all, not expensive. Rents are affordable and there are seven student dormitories in the immediate vicinity of the campus. Likewise, the numerous shopping opportunities allow for a complete supply, because in Amberg you can find everything - from boutiques to discounters - and that at an affordable cost of living.

For your health, the city of Amberg offers everything you need. Doctors of the most important specialties are located here. The St. Marien Clinic is equipped with modern facilities and has very well-trained staff.

In addition to your studies, leisure activities naturally play an important role for you. You can find out about the cultural offerings, the beautiful old town with its high density of pubs and other municipal facilities in Amberg here.

## Economy

As part of the Nuremberg metropolitan region, the economy in Amberg is represented by numerous companies. Some world market leaders operate a branch in the Bavarian upper center.

Students in Amberg have numerous opportunities to get in touch with these companies in internships, student research projects or as working students. Almost 80 percent of our alumni have gone directly to companies in the region. You can find out more about the major employers and listed companies here (https://amberg.de/rathaus/standortprofil/die-groessten-arbeitgeber-in-amberg) .

Here (https://idp1.oth-aw.de/idp/profile/SAML2/Redirect/SSO?execution=e1s1) you can find out which companies within the region or close to our university is part of our OTH Amberg-Weiden PartnerCircle.

Adresse:

Hetzenrichter Weg 15
92637 Weiden

## Why to study in Weiden?

Weiden is a cosmopolitan city in the northern Upper Palatinate with infrastructural links to the Czech Republic and the administrative district of Upper Franconia. Our campus for the faculties of business administration and industrial engineering is also located here.

And this location has grown steadily in recent years - equipment and buildings are state-of-the-art. For our students, this means modern (IT) laboratories, lecture halls and library, so that project work, presentations and research activities can be carried out in the best possible way. What additionally distinguishes Weiden as a university location is the familiar atmosphere between students and the direct contact to lecturers and staff.

Adjacent to our buildings at the Weiden site, as the crow flies, is the student dormitory at the Postkeller, 50 meters away. Another dormitory is also only 500 meters away from the campus. If you want your own apartment, you can also settle outside the student dormitories thanks to the fair rental prices.

One of the highlights of Weiden is the old town. Historic buildings form the backdrop for countless shopping opportunities and places to eat. The city also offers a wide range of cultural activities. Great events, a diverse nightlife and other events round out the overall package. Here you will find detailed information about Weiden's cultural offerings.

## Economy

Weiden is the economic center of the northern Upper Palatinate. A large number of companies are located within a radius of 50 kilometers. These range from world market leaders in the mechanical engineering and logistics sectors to numerous global players in the automotive sector and well-known trading companies.

Our university's cooperation with these companies enables you to gain practical experience and also offers you numerous career opportunities after your academic education. Hand in hand, we stand with regional companies for the goal: "High-quality education of top performers from the region for the economy of the Upper Palatinate and beyond."

## About us

The Institute for Medical Technology (IfMZ) is a scientific research institution at the Ostbayerische Technische Hochschule Amberg-Weiden (OTH Amberg-Weiden). As a central interface, the IfMZ connects all university-related activities between research, teaching, and industry in the field of medical technology.

With a working group of professors, scientists, and engineers from diverse specializations, the institute has access to a broad range of expertise in the fields of medicine, molecular biology, and engineering. In close collaboration with regional and national external partners, the IfMZ integrates questions from applied medical technology research with the practical training of highly qualified specialists for the future-oriented field of medical technology. The institute cooperates with numerous companies in the medical technology industry, hospitals, specialist medical practices, and external research institutions.

## Business administration - do your thing in business & management

How do successful companies operate—and what does it take to keep them on track financially? From pricing in supermarkets to production planning in industrial settings, from human resources management to international expansion: business administration is all around us. That’s exactly what makes the Business Administration program so exciting, versatile, and relevant! You’ll learn how companies operate, how markets evolve, and how to manage a business responsibly in an increasingly interconnected world.

Your curriculum will cover topics such as accounting, marketing, human resources management, business law, and finance. You’ll develop a keen understanding of economic relationships—while also honing your skills in communication, leadership, and teamwork.

With its strong practical focus, small class sizes, and real-world business projects , the program at OTH Amberg-Weiden offers you the perfect blend of theory and practice. This ensures that, upon graduation, you’ll be fully prepared for challenging roles in business, administration, or even in starting your own company.

## Career prospects

With your degree in business administration, numerous doors are open to you - in almost every industry and all over the world. Depending on which specialization you choose, you can work as a:

- Marketing expert in agencies or industrial companies
- Management consultant with a global player
- Specialist in auditing or tax consulting
- Controller or in financial analysis
- Project or sales manager at home or abroad

Want even more? Then add on a Master's degree - we have a wide range of options here. Or you can go your own way: many of our graduates have successfully founded their own companies - with ideas that they developed during their studies. We support you with know-how, workshops and personal advice.

## VERY GOOD RATINGS - VERY GOOD PROSPECTS

At OTH Amberg-Weiden, we combine sound theory with practical learning. Small groups, modern facilities, personal support and close cooperation with companies create the best study conditions.
This is also confirmed by the excellent StudyCheck ratings and the success of our graduates. Those who study here are well prepared for the future.

Study-Check Ratings (https://www.studycheck.de/hochschulen/oth-aw)

## HIGHLIGHTS of the course

Instead of memorizing dry theory, you will develop practical solutions for real challenges from the corporate world on the business administration degree course at OTH Amberg-Weiden. Instead of analyzing fictitious case studies, you will work together with fellow students on projects with regional and international companies - always with the aim of delivering concrete results that are really needed. Instead of struggling through overcrowded lecture halls, you benefit from small groups, personal support and a modern learning environment.

What makes the course special is the close connection to practice : you don't just learn business fundamentals, you apply them directly - in project work, workshops and interactive teaching formats. In this way, you not only develop specialist knowledge, but also team spirit, creativity and problem-solving skills - all skills that are in high demand in business . And this is exactly what makes our business studies course a real career turbo.

## Certification Programmes

In addition to your regular studies, you can take certification courses at OTH Amberg-Weiden free of charge - for example in the areas of project management or digitalisation. These additional qualifications are a real plus for your CV and help you to position yourself specifically in your professional field. You can find an overview of all certificates here:

Certifications

## Structure

In the Business Administration (B.A.) program at OTH Amberg-Weiden, you’ll earn 210 ECTS credits over seven semesters and gain everything you need to understand business contexts and make informed decisions in a corporate setting. You’ll take courses on the fundamentals of economics, such as finance and investment, business mathematics, statistics, and macroeconomics. Key areas such as marketing, law, controlling, and logistics are also on your schedule.
You’ll gain valuable practical experience through projects with companies, where you’ll work with your team to tackle real-world problems —and develop solutions that are actually implemented. Additionally, you’ll strengthen important personal skills in modules on communication, teamwork, and academic research.

Customize or specialize your profile:
Starting in the fourth semester, you’ll build your personal competency profile: You can either freely combine courses from a wide range of electives to become a generalist—or you can choose a specific competency profile to specialize.
Bonus: If you complete all the modules in a competency profile, you’ll receive an official certificate in addition to your bachelor’s degree—a strong asset for your resume and potential employers.
In the sixth semester, you’ll apply your knowledge directly in a company setting during an internship. And in the seventh semester, you’ll write your bachelor’s thesis—ideally on a specific real-world problem.

General Information:

Mechanical Engineering is not only concerned with development, design and optimization. It also means getting others excited about your ideas. That’s why the programme combines engineering and business skills. Skills that enable you to take on a leadership role in a technology-oriented company. A compulsory work placement and practical project work in the University’s modern state-of-the-art laboratories ensure that theoretical knowledge can be put into practice right from the start. It also allows sufficient flexibility for further specialisation in areas of individual interest, such as Automotive Engineering, Laser Technology, Production Engineering or Polymer Technology.

Degree: BEng

Duration: 3 years

Start of studies: winter (October 1) and summer (March 15)

Application period: May 1 through July 15 for the winter term, November 20 through January 15 for the summer term

Entrance requirements:

General entrance qualification for admission to a university or technical college or a subject-related university entrance qualification. Admission is also possible via professional university access. Students have to serve a pre-study internship of at least twelve weeks in a relevant professional field prior to their studies or by the end of the third semester at the latest.

German B2 (language of instruction: German)

Contents and Structure:

The programme is divided into three module groups.

The first group , Fundamentals of Mathematics and Science , consists of the following modules:

- Mathematics
- Physics and Chemistry
- Computer Science for Engineers

The second group, Fundamentals of Engineering , provides engineering-related course content, such as

- Technical Mechanics
- Material Science
- Strength of Materials
- Machine Parts I
- Development and Design I
- Electrical Engineering I
- Dynamics of Machines
- Technical Thermodynamics
- Technical Fluid Mechanics
- Control Engineering

The third group, Applied Engineering , involves the following topics:

- Development and Design II
- Machine Parts II
- Manufacturing Technology and Quality Assurance
- Plastics Engineering
- Electrical Engineering II
- Measurement Technology
- Energy Conversion in Engines and Machines

In the 6 th and 7thsemester, students may choose one of the following areas of specialisation :

- Automotive Engineering
- Laser Technology
- Production Engineering
- Polymer Technology

The last semester is designated for the completion of the final research paper (Bachelor’s Thesis) which may also cover research carried out in connection with practical placement at a company.

## MEDICAL ENGINEERING – BRING TECHNOLOGY CLOSER TO THE PUBLIC!

Medicine without technology? Unthinkable! From hearing aids to pacemakers, from MRI scanners to hybrid operating theatres, from hygiene to laboratory analyses - the expertise, experience and innovative strength of medical engineering are everywhere. That's what makes the Medical Engineering degree programme so exciting and varied! Because you acquire broad, interdisciplinary knowledge . Your degree programme includes scientific , precision engineering , electrical engineering and medical subjects .

With demographic change and more and more chronic illnesses, medical engineering is becoming increasingly important! The content of the degree programme is therefore tailored to current requirements and future technologies . This will make you a sought-after specialist after graduation!

## Career Opportunities

Many career paths are open to you after you graduate: You can work

- in hospitals
- in the medical industry or
- research institutions .

There you will develop and design medical products, design and maintain devices, work in sales, consulting, quality assurance and much more. Or you can gain further qualifications and complete your Master's degree which you can also complete here!

MASTER MEDIcal Engineering

## HIGHLIGHTS OF THE DEGREE PROGRAMME

Instead of poring over dry theory in a lecture hall, at the OTH Amberg-Weiden you will gain invaluable practical experience , learn how to design a medical technology product using modern digital development methods , and even print out your design in the 3D printing lab .

You will apply manufacturing processes for medical technology in a clean room and also have the opportunity to gain further qualification with a radiation protection course . Excursions will take you to a wide variety of areas in medical technology, from industrial production to hospital applications.

The list could go on, but these examples alone make it clear: if you study Medical Engineering at OTH Amberg-Weiden, you will not only learn the theory, but above all gain sought-after practical skills, making you a skilled specialist in the constantly growing medical industry!

OTH Amberg-Weiden stands out above all for its

- Practice-oriented training ,
- Modern laboratory equipment and
- Various areas of specialization

## STRUCTURE & DOCUMENTS

In the technical part of the degree programme, you will learn the basics such as mathematics or CAD, as well as advanced topics such as data science, automation or robotics. The management part of the programme focuses on business management skills in the industrial sector, such as business process management or marketing and sales. On the one hand, you will acquire interdisciplinary language skills, but also deal with overarching disciplines such as logistics or software development.

In the final stage of your studies, you can choose your own modules from a wide-ranging catalogue and thus determine your own specialisations.

For example, during an excursion to a clinic or a student research project together with a medical device manufacturer. Or during your practical semester . This is compulsory on every Bachelor's degree programme at OTH Amberg-Weiden. Here you gain your first professional experience, can apply your knowledge in practice and make important contacts with potential future employers .

## Industrial Engineering - Two in one: Technology and Business Administration

The requirements in business are very complex: engineers can assess the technical aspects of a new product, while business economists can think through economic issues. But business economists and engineers do not always speak the same language.

This is where you come in - after studying Industrial Engineering at OTH Amberg-Weiden, you will know how to create solution-oriented and innovative approaches as a link between technology and business.

Based on the German Qualifications Framework, you will benefit from an interdisciplinary education in engineering and business subjects, technology and management.

From the 6th semester onwards, you can set your own personal focus and decide on a specialisation.You can choose from the following:

- Digital product development
- Digitalisation in production and logistics

## CAREER OPPORTUNITIES

The electrical and automation industry as well as mechanical and plant engineering are sectors of the future par excellence and traditionally a backbone of German industry, whose companies occupy leading positions worldwide. In order to maintain this position, industrial engineers are indispensable and are consequently among the top earners among all academics.

Core industries and main areas of employment for industrial engineers are

- Automotive industry
- Aircraft and spacecraft construction
- Energy technology
- Information and communication technology
- Medical technology
- Logistics
- Research and development
- Technical services
- Machines and special machine construction
- Construction industry

## HIGHLIGHTS OF THE DEGREE PROGRAMME

The Industrial Engineering and Management degree programme at the OTH in Weiden is characterised by small study groups and thus the opportunity for intensive cooperation between students and lecturers.

The Faculty of Industrial Engineering is characterised by a personal environment, a lively partner network, international contacts and close proximity to important regional companies.

We attach great importance to a high degree of practical relevance in our degree programmes. Project work gives you the opportunity to answer and implement practical questions. Our students almost always write their final thesis in a company and thus make their first contacts with a potential employer.

The demand for our graduates remains high.

## STRUCTURE & DOCUMENTS

The full-time programme takes seven semesters and has three phases: fundamentals, practical semester and your personal profile. Practical relevance is a given: in modern laboratories, through project work and on excursions, you deepen your knowledge using real examples.

- Semesters 1 to 4: Fundamentals. All students take the same 24 compulsory modules from three areas:
- Engineering and natural sciences: Mathematics, Statistics, Physics, Engineering Mechanics, Engineering Design, Materials and Manufacturing Technology, Electrical Engineering, Automation Technology, Programming, Computer Science and Databases
- Business: Business Administration, Accounting, Finance and Investment, Marketing and Sales, Process Management, Business Law, Economics
- Interdisciplinary: English, Logistics, Industrial Engineering, Project Management and Agile Methods

- Semester 5: Practical semester. You work for 22 weeks in a company, abroad if you wish.
- Semesters 6 and 7: Your profile. You choose ten elective modules and write your bachelor's thesis, often in cooperation with a company.

### Elective modules and specialisations

In the 6th and 7th semesters, you put together your own programme. You choose ten modules from a catalogue of more than 25, including at least two each from engineering, business and interdisciplinary topics. A practical project in a company can replace one elective module.

If you want to specialise, you choose modules from one of six specialisations and can receive a certificate:

- Digital Product Development
- Digitalisation in Production and Logistics
- Ethics and Sustainability
- Process Management and Data Analysis
- Technical Procurement and Sales
- Digital Processes and Applications

The table below shows which elective modules belong to which specialisation.

### Dual Study Programme

Would you like to work for a company while you study? Then a dual study programme may be right for you. There are two models:

- Combined study and vocational training (Verbundstudium): You also complete vocational training and earn two qualifications.
- Study with in-depth practice (Studium mit vertiefter Praxis): You study as normal and also work in longer practical phases at the company.

In both models, you are at the university during the lecture period and at the company during the lecture-free period. You also complete your practical semester and your bachelor's thesis there.

You need a contract with a company. You can find partner companies and open places for Industrial Engineering at hochschule dual, the initiative of the Bavarian universities for dual study (in German):

- Industrial Engineering, combined study and vocational training (https://www.hochschule-dual.de/studiengaenge/details/wirtschaftsingenieurwesen-verbundstudium-ausbildungsintegrierend-ostbayerische-technische-hochschule-amberg-weiden)
- Industrial Engineering, study with in-depth practice (https://www.hochschule-dual.de/studiengaenge/details/wirtschaftsingenieurwesen-studium-mit-vertiefter-praxis-praxisintegrierend-ostbayerische-technische-hochschule-amberg-weiden)

The page Dual Study Programme at OTH Amberg-Weiden explains how to apply and who will be glad to answer your questions.

## PRACTICAL REFERENCE

All of our professors come from industry and bring with them current topics from operational practice.

## Description

The master's degree program "Applied Research in Engineering Sciences" (M-APR) offers bachelor's and diploma graduates the opportunity to obtain higher qualifications in applied research and development. The study program is closely linked to a research project and is accompanied by in-depth courses tailored to the respective project. During the entire duration of the study program, students are supervised by an appointed professor. The program qualifies students to work independently in engineering on application-oriented research projects. In addition to the technical content, students also become familiar with organizational processes as they occur in complex cross-company projects (e.g. in national or European research projects).

The master's program "Applied Research in Engineering Sciences" is an independent program of the OTH Amberg-Weiden. It is offered in cooperation with the following universities (joint seminar offers and conferences):

- East Bavarian Technical University (OTH) Amberg-Weiden

Have you completed your bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering or a Mechanical Engineering-specific discipline with above-average grades? Then expand your knowledge now. With the master's degree program "Innovation-focussed Engineering and Management" you will deepen the contents and open up newly advanced technology areas. This is the ideal starting point for developing products and seeing them through to market maturity. Of course, with a master's degree you can also take on the role of project manager or work in corporate management. A master's degree is also a prerequisite for a scientific career with a doctorate. Maybe you even have an innovative idea and want to start your own company?
We will support you in achieving your professional goals: In the course of your master's studies, you will gain sound technical know-how to develop products and machines. In lectures on technology management and innovation management you will learn how to implement innovative ideas and drive projects forward in companies. You will deepen and expand this theoretical knowledge at and with our industry partners. In addition, you will acquire knowledge in management and patent research during the master's program.

In this program, you have the choice between the areas of specialization: simulation or laser technology.

Internationalization has radically changed business and industry. In order to operate on the global market, companies need highly trained specialists: employees with enormous expertise, good language skills and intercultural competencies. In short: employees with a Master's degree in Intercultural Business and Technology Management.

This degree program is interdisciplinary. You will learn more about technological developments, business and economic contexts, and the importance of cultural factors in international business. But most importantly: you will learn how to link these different aspects. This holistic perspective is important in order to grasp processes and structures in their entirety and align them to a common goal.

In order for you to move confidently on the international stage, we promote your social competence, willingness to cooperate and communication skills during your studies. This will enable you to work successfully in international teams and take on management tasks later on.

Have you completed an interdisciplinary bachelor's degree with technological and economic components, such as Industrial Engineering or International Technology Management? Then this degree program is the perfect complement. The master's program is also open to you if you have completed a business or technical degree.

Take off on the global market - with the master's program in Intercultural Business and Technology Management!

Do you want to take on management responsibility in healthcare and life-science companies or medical and scientific institutions? Then enrol in the Master's program in Medical Technology.

Medical technology is the industry of the future: Due to demographic developments, the market for medical products is constantly expanding. As the industrialization gathers pace, the demand is also increasing in emerging markets. At the same time, the digital transformation is revolutionizing medical technology. Artificial intelligence, big data and the like are opening up new markets in the field of medial technology.

With a master's degree in Medical Engineering, you will become part of this highly innovative market – and well prepared for a leadership role in national or international companies.

The degree program provides you with the ability to take on tasks in various areas of activity both in nationally or internationally operating medical-technical companies.

content:

Section: Studies Study offers Study programmes

### Economy and Law (Study Location Aschaffenburg)

Studienort: Aschaffenburg (https://www.th-ab.de/)

Do you like to juggle numbers or paragraphs? Are you no stranger to terms like mergers & acquisitions and tax structuring? Would you like to learn more about how the world of credit business works or are you interested in tax law issues? Perhaps you already work in financial management or tax consulting?

Then the Economics and Law program is the right choice for you to deepen your knowledge and skills from your bachelor's or diploma studies specifically in the area of finance or tax law and auditing!

The master's program is a cooperative project between the OTH Amberg-Weiden and the Aschaffenburg University of Applied Sciences and combines the competencies and specific strengths of the lecturers of either institution. With its focus on finance, tax law and auditing, the Economics and Law program offers you a market-oriented study program with topicality and high standards covering the whole range of the areas of finance, tax law and auditing.

This program trains you to become highly qualified specialists and managers for companies in all sectors, especially banks and corporations, as well as for nationally and internationally active auditing or consulting firms.

The course is offered to graduates of Business Administration, Business Administration and Law or graduates of related fields.

The central study location for the entire duration of the program is Aschaffenburg University of Applied Sciences.

The program concludes with the academic degree Master of Arts, Master of Science or Master of Laws.

Welcome to OTH Amberg-Weiden!

Here you will find all the important information for successfully starting your studies.
Please note: Important dates will be added on a regular basis.

You still have some questions?
You will find the corresponding contact person directly with each link.
But please make sure to read the information first.

## Information for first semester students

Beginning is not that hard... And with our help and support, you will quickly find your way around the university.
And, of course, there are also online events, workshops and preparation courses designed to make starting easier.

## First Semester Welcome

Dear First-Semester Students,
A warm welcome to OTH Amberg-Weiden!

The first-semester orientation will take place on Thursday, October 1, 2026 (please check whether you are studying at the Amberg campus or the Weiden campus).

At the event, you’ll receive important information about your studies. You’ll also get to know your fellow students, students from higher semesters, your professors, and key contacts at the university. All enrolled students will receive an invitation with all the information and details before the event.

Students from higher semesters are also warmly invited to the Welcome Party !

The following schedule is planned:

15.30 Uhr | Spiritual Reflection to Kick Off the Academic Year (optional)
Amberg: Musikomm (Fleurystraße 1, 92224 Amberg)
Weiden: Campus OTH Amberg-Weiden, Hetzenrichter Weg 15, 92637 Weiden (Multifunction Room in the Hörsaalgebäude) | 16.00 Uhr | Official Welcome Event for First-Year Students
Amberg: Musikomm
Weiden: Hörsaalgebäude (H001) | ab 16:30 | Study-Programme Introductions and Campus Tour | Then: | Welcome Party (Get-together) with students, “Prof. on the Sofa,” music, and refreshments
Amberg: Musikomm
Weiden: Mensa

The rooms in Weiden are marked on the campus plan . The Musikomm in Amberg is located right next to the campus and is within walking distance. All event venues are clearly marked. You can use the university’s parking facilities at both locations.

Lectures for the winter semester of 2026 will begin for all students on Friday, October 2, 2026. Any questions? Please feel free to contact studienberatung@oth-aw.de .

### We wish you a good start and a successful semester!

## International Students Club (ISC) and its Buddy Program

The ISC is a student-organised body of the International Office and active both at the campus in Amberg and in Weiden.

The main goal is simple: the ISC wants to promote contact between OTH’s international and German students. Students from all over the world should feel welcome and at home at OTH AW. To achieve this, the team does not only organise regular events on site, but also organises various excursions near and far.

The ISC would like to be a place to make friends and experience new things together, a place of mutual respect and togetherness. Plus, they also want to encourage German students to venture abroad and serve as an informal contact point for international students.

More Information on the ISC

International Buddy Program

The International Buddy Program enables international students of OTH AW to get to know German students and to have contact persons for questions and problems that arise. Further, German students who are interested in international and intercultural exchange have the opportunity to meet students from all over the world.

Buddies are committed students who are interested in international exchange and who help international students during the semester. Activities of the buddies are for example the support by dealing with authorities and help with questions/problems that arise during the daily study life.

Are you interested in becoming a Buddy or would you like to get supported as an international student?
Then get in touch with us :)
