## Artificial intelligence - make machines think!

Become a specialist in the innovative development of intelligent, self-learning applications with a deep understanding of artificial and human intelligence. Join us at OTH Amberg-Weiden, where this state-of-the-art degree program is offered across all faculties at the Amberg location. Develop machine learning methods from huge amounts of data and solve complex challenges with artificial intelligence. Program industrial robots and experiment with the "AI" of computer games. Become an expert in visual and linguistic intelligence and develop ubiquitous, mobile applications for the "smart home" in the "smart city".

## Career opportunities

Artificial intelligence is a highly topical and at the same time forward-looking megatrend, which is already as old as computer science, but which will decisively shape our future, especially due to the progress in " Deep Learning ". Worldwide, but also in our region, AI experts are sought after in almost all areas of life, application and industry.

## Study models

The bachelor's degree program in Artificial Intelligence can be completed as a full-time program. Your studies include six theoretical semesters and one practical semester in which you gain insights into later professional life and can make valuable contacts for your career at an early stage.

The lectures are supplemented and deepened by internships, project work and social group learning units. After successful completion, you will receive the title Bachelor of Science (B.Sc.).

## Application

#### Study start

It is currently only possible to start the Artificial Intelligence (AI) course in the winter semester. An additional start for the summer semester is currently being planned.

#### Application dates

You can apply online for the program from May 1 to July 15 of each year. In exceptional cases, we extend the application deadlines for individual degree programs. You can find out whether you can still apply for this degree program in the applicant portal (https://www3.primuss.de/cgi-bin/bew_anmeldung_v2/index.pl) .

#### Admission requirements

Would you like to apply for the Artificial Intelligence (AI) degree program? For admission to the OTH Amberg-Weiden, you need a general higher education entrance qualification, a subject-specific higher education entrance qualification or a technical college entrance qualification. Admission is also possible via the vocational university entrance qualification.

## Aufbau Künstliche Intelligenz

As a student of Artificial Intelligence, you are a specialist in the development of interactive and self-learning applications with a deep understanding of human processes, behavior and perception. You will design and develop AI applications that use machine learning, draw on huge amounts of data, solve complex problems or can be used in robotics. You will also be an expert in AI-supported image, speech and sensor signal processing. You will acquire the knowledge for these diverse tasks on the Artificial Intelligence degree program at OTH Amberg-Weiden.

## Inhalte

Artificial intelligence is present in almost all areas of our lives today. Knowledge from this specialist field is used in a wide range of different application areas. The Artificial Intelligence degree course teaches these topics, among others:

Data Analytics & Computer Vision

Data analysis techniques or "data analytics" are penetrating the world of science and business at a rapid pace. Deep learning algorithms in particular are driving innovation and performance improvements in artificial intelligence. Data analytics is an established and accepted field that is being used enthusiastically in both science and business.

This knowledge is combined with the specialist and research field of computer vision. Here, knowledge of computer science is closely interlinked with that of engineering. Visual information is first processed and analyzed. Various methods are used to automate the understanding of visual content and extract relevant information for further processing. Computer-based vision is not only used in many existing industries, but also enables the creation of innovative new areas.

Smart Energy and Smart Home

The change in energy supply towards decentralized and renewable generation structures is a current challenge not only in Germany. Our future lies in an environmentally friendly and economical energy supply. However, in addition to applications in the energy supply sector, there is also a direct need in households.

Smart energy and smart home are no longer unknown terms. Rather, they include topics relating to energy transmission, energy consumption, energy generation, energy use, increasing the quality of living and quality of life, using intelligent processes that can ensure both safety and efficiency.

The technologies developed in this way are among the key disciplines of artificial intelligence. They are therefore a focus of the Artificial Intelligence degree program at OTH Amberg-Weiden.

Smart Robotics & Smart Media

The field of robotics has developed strongly in recent years. There is an increasing demand for highly flexible robot solutions for the markets. These not only reduce costs but also support unique selling points and are efficient helpers for every team. Smat Robotics focuses on the new technologies in robotics.

In combination with Smart Media, knowledge is imparted that enables innovative media developments. The latest technological concepts lead to entire living environments being supported by media and made future-proof in the interests of people. In this context, smart means the interaction of the latest technology with innovative media implementation in order to optimally support people in the most diverse areas of life.

## Course of study

Your studies usually last seven semesters and lead to the academic degree "Bachelor of Science in Artificial Intelligence".

The Bachelor's degree program in Artificial Intelligence is divided into three study sections. The first two semesters provide basic knowledge and include the following modules:

- theoretical and practical computer science
- Mathematics and revision
- Python programming
- Ethics and interaction
- classical AI
- Stochastics
- English & Web
- C & C++

In the first two semesters of the second stage of studies (semesters 3 and 4), the basics are deepened and the practical phase is prepared:

- Java and Java Script programming
- Data engineering and data analytics
- Mobile and ubiquitous computing
- Algorithms and data structures
- Machine learning
- Cloud and NoSQL
- Computer vision
- Big Data

The second study phase ends with the completion of the practical phase in a company in semester 5.

In the third and final stage of the course (semesters 6 and 7), the following courses turn future graduates into specialists in the field of artificial intelligence:

- Artificial Intelligence and Innovation
- Specialization
- Deep Learning
- Electives
- Bachelor's seminar and Bachelor's thesis.

## International Management & Sustainability - Make sustainability your thing

Global economy without responsibility? Unthinkable! Companies worldwide are faced with the challenge of being economically successful - and at the same time acting in a sustainable, fair and future-orientated way . This is exactly where the International Management & Sustainability Master's degree programme comes in: you combine international management expertise with a focus on ecological, social and economic sustainability.

Your timetable includes topics such as strategic management, global value chains, environmental economics, project management and corporate social responsibility. You will develop yourself further - professionally, linguistically and personally - and acquire precisely the skills that are in demand in international contexts and non-profit non-governmental organisations (NGOs).

With English-language teaching, intercultural exchange, small groups and practical projects, the degree programme at OTH Amberg-Weiden offers you the ideal framework for effectively combining sustainability and management .

## Career prospects

With your Master's degree in International Management & Sustainability, exciting career paths are open to you worldwide - in companies, international organisations, associations or foundations. You will be ideally prepared to think holistically about economic processes, understand global interrelationships and actively help shape sustainable strategies.

After graduating, you can work as a:

- Sustainability manager in industrial or service companies
- Project manager in an international environment
- Expert in corporate responsibility or environmental economics
- Manager in purchasing, sales, production or controlling
- Team leader in intercultural organisations or NGO projects
- Consultant for sustainable transformation and international expansion

Your profile is international, practical, and forward-looking—with in-depth subject knowledge, intercultural competence, and strong leadership skills. Want even more? Many of our graduates have successfully launched their own businesses—based on ideas they developed while still in school. We support you in this endeavor with expertise, workshops, and personalized guidance. You can find more information here:

STARTUP CONSULTING

## VERY GOOD RATINGS - VERY GOOD PROSPECTS

At OTH Amberg-Weiden, we combine sound theory with practical learning. Small groups, modern facilities, personal support and close cooperation with companies create the best study conditions.
This is also confirmed by the excellent StudyCheck ratings and the success of our graduates. Those who study here are well prepared for the future.

Study-Check Ratings (https://www.studycheck.de/hochschulen/oth-aw)

## HIGHLIGHTS of the course

Instead of just learning theories from textbooks, on the Master's degree programme in International Management & Sustainability you will deal with real challenges from international business practice - always with a focus on sustainable business. Instead of discussing purely abstract concepts, you will work in a team to develop concrete solutions for global issues in management , environmental economics or social entrepreneurship.

Instead of sitting in overcrowded lecture theatres, you study in small groups with personal support - and learn in an international, English-speaking environment that promotes intercultural skills and creates space for exchange.

What makes the degree programme special is the combination of management and sustainability, practice and science , global thinking and responsible action . The programme not only prepares you for your career, but also for the challenges of a changing world.

## Certification Programmes

In addition to your regular studies, you can take certification courses at OTH Amberg-Weiden free of charge - for example in the areas of project management or digitalisation. These additional qualifications are a real plus for your CV and help you to position yourself specifically in your professional field. You can find an overview of all certificates here:

Certifications

## Structure

On the Master's degree programme in International Management & Sustainability, you will deepen your knowledge of international management issues and sustainable corporate management . Your timetable includes topics such as strategic management, global value chains, intercultural management and business ethics - supplemented by content such as environmental economics, corporate sustainability and climate change.

Instead of just analysing what responsibility means in theory, you will develop concrete solutions for real challenges in practical projects - for example in the areas of social entrepreneurship or sustainable innovation. You will also strengthen your personal skills in electives such as Organisational Psychology, Design Thinking or Compliance & CSR.

In the third semester, you will apply your skills in a service-learning project and write your Master's thesis - ideally linked to a specific practical or research topic. Upon successful completion, you will be awarded the academic degree of Master of Arts (M.A.).

# Application Information (M.A. International Management & Sustainability)

## Access and admission requirements

Please note: Statements about eligibility cannot be given in advance! You have to go through the application process to have your documents reviewed ( online admissions portal (https://www3.primuss.de/cgi-bin/bew_anmeldung_v2/index.pl) ). For a smooth process, international applicants should apply 6-8 weeks before the end of the application period if possible.

The Master's program in International Management & Sustainability is aimed at prospective students who have completed their Bachelor's or Diploma studies in a course of study considered relevant. Relevant courses of study are, in addition to business administration-oriented courses of study, in particular interdisciplinary courses of study with elements from social or cultural science courses of study (e.g. International Business, Applied Business Psychology, Digital Business, International Technology Management) as well as, technology-oriented courses with management content (e.g. Industrial Engineering, Media Informatics). However, study programs with an overwhelming focus on engineering subjects are not considered relevant . The university degree must have been completed with an overall examination performance of "good" or better (minimum of a 2.5 grade average, German grading system; for information on the German grading system, please refer to (Link under construction)). The entry and admission requirements for the Master's program as well as information on the aptitude test can be found in the study and examination regulations for the program (https://www.oth-aw.de/files/oth-aw/Studiengaenge/Master/IMS/Studiengangsseite/SPO_IMS_WS2122_convenience_translation.pdf) .

In addition, a sufficient knowledge of the English language must be proven by a language certificate corresponding to level B2 according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages. One of the following English language tests with the specified minimum score is sufficient: TOEFL IBT - 80 / IELTS Cambridge - 6 / TOEIC - 780. Proof is not required if the university entrance qualification or university degree was obtained in English. Proof of German language skills at level A2 must be submitted before you begin your studies, i.e. latest at the time of your official enrolment. This is obviously not required if your previous studies or university entrance qualification were completed in German. Accepted certificates are: Goethe-certificate, telc, ÖSD-certificate. During the master's program, German language skills must be expanded to level B1 (e.g. through German courses, internships or self-study).

As stated above, the Master's program International Management & Sustainability requires the passing of an aptitude test in the form of a written essay . Here are details about your task:

- Write an essay on the below mentioned topic in the field of international management and sustainability
- Language of the essay: English
- Length of the essay: Minimum of 1000 words and maximum of 1500 words
- Submit your essay electronically via the online admissions portal PRIMUSS (https://www3.primuss.de/cgi-bin/bew_anmeldung_v2/index.pl)
- All external sources used must be indicated
- An additional confirmation should testify that the essay was written personally by you

Essay topic:
Why is the topic of International Management & Sustainability of importance to you? Please share a personal experience or an issue that bothers you related to questions of international management and/or to questions of sustainability and how you deal/dealt with it. If suitable, use concepts/theoretical models from the respective fields.

The evaluation criteria of the essay are equally the quality of the content and the formal quality of the argumentation related to the structures of scientific analysis and linguistic expression.

(POC: Susanne Winterl & Uni-assist (https://my.uni-assist.de/hilfe) )
All international applicants (including citizens of EU-member states) who have not obtained their higher education entrance qualification (i.e. secondary-school leaving certificate) in Germany must have their credentials reviewed and approved by uni-assist (http://www.uni-assist.de/) . Please note that it can take up to several weeks until you receive your VPD (Vorprüfungsdokumentation = necessary document for your application). ####

## Do I need a visa if I want to study at OTH Amberg-Weiden?

(POC: Susanne Winterl )

####

## What are the application requirements?

(POC: Theresa Schreiber and Susanne Winterl )

(POC: Susanne Winterl )

Proof of German A2 must be submitted before you begin your studies, i.e. latest at the time of your official enrolment. Information about requirements for our study program International Management & Sustainability can be found on the pages "Access and admission restrictions" of the programme .

One of the following English language tests with minimum scores as indicated will be sufficient:

- TOEFEL IBT - 80
- IELTS Cambridge - 6
- TOEIC – 780

Unfortunately, we cannot make any statements about eligibility in advance. Please upload your documents for the application process
and the examination board will then decide whether you can be admitted.

title: More flexible part-time studying (1/2)
content:
More flexible part-time studying
Section: Studies Study offers Forms of study

# More flexible part-time studying

Childcare, caring for relatives, permanent job or desire for flexible offers/work-life balance - more and more people want or need to balance their academic education and training with other factors. For many, a part-time study model with a smaller amount of teaching and learning units per semester is an option. OTH Amberg-Weiden will be offering a part-time Bachelor's programme for the degree programmes from the winter semester 2020/21:

- International Technology Management
- Medical Engineering
- Industrial Engineering

In terms of content, part-time study is identical to full-time study, only the structure and procedure are different: students acquire an average of 20 ECTS credits per semester instead of 30, i.e. less workload per semester. The standard period of study is stretched to 11 semesters.
After individual assessment, full-time study is possible at any time with crediting of the acquired achievements, and the study programme is shortened accordingly.

Questions about application and admission? The students’ office is happy to help.

## Our part-time study courses

## FAQ

### General

####

The part-time study model at OTH Amberg-Weiden means that students earn an average of 20 ECTS credits per semester, i.e. they have a lower workload per semester. For comparison: In the full-time course, a semester is usually completed with 30 ECTS points.

The content as well as the study and examination achievements do not differ from the full-time course. As a result, a total of 210 ECTS credits are acquired in an extended standard period of study of 11 semesters. The bachelor’s degree is awarded upon successful completion of the course.

### Schedule of studies

####

This depends on the degree programme you choose. If this programme provides for specializations/focus areas, you must choose one in accordance with the study and examination regulations.

####

Part-time students are integrated into the full-time curriculum. They attend the same courses as students on the full-time course, but with fewer modules per semester. As a rule, lectures take place Monday to Friday in the mornings and afternoons.

####

In the first few semesters, the basic subjects provide the necessary technical foundation for your training. Depending on your chosen degree course, after the practical phase you decide on your preferred specialization and deepen your specialist knowledge. In the integrated practical phase, you will complete an extensive industrial internship in a company or institution.

In the full-time program, the practical phase comprises an internship of 100 working days, which should be completed in one continuous period. In part-time studies, this corresponds to an equivalent of 100 working days, which can be spread over two semesters, provided the internship provider allows this. By submitting an informal application, you can also combine the practical phase and complete it full-time in one semester if the 100 working days are completed full-time in this semester. The standard period of study is shortened by one semester accordingly. In the eleventh semester, you usually complete your studies by writing your bachelor’s thesis.

####

The weekly attendance time for part-time students is around 9-12 hours of 45 minutes each. In addition, there is time for preparing and following up on courses, possible group work outside the courses and time for self-study.

Part-time study is easily compatible with (flexible) employment of around 20-25 hours/week. However, students are expected to show a certain flexibility and willingness to adapt their working hours to the course times. Employers must also expect that working hours may change each semester.

####

No. Part-time students choose their courses from the same range of courses as full-time students. OTH Amberg-Weiden strives to adapt the teaching times to the needs of the students.

Please bear in mind that, unlike working professional students, your lecture times will not be in the evenings or at weekends.

####

Winter semester: from the beginning of October to mid-March, the exams usually take place in the first weeks of the lecture-free period from mid/end of January. Lectures are held from October until the beginning of the lecture-free period.

Summer semester: from mid-March to the end of September, examinations usually take place in the first weeks of the lecture-free period from the beginning/mid-July. Lectures are held from mid-March until the beginning of the lecture-free period.

####

You can find all information on courses and lecture times on our website under the relevant degree program. Once you have received your letter of admission, you can draw up your semester timetable and coordinate the times with your employer or childcare facilities if necessary. The Student Advisory Service will be happy to help you with your planning.

### Financial

####

According to the current legal situation, part-time students are not entitled to BAföG funding (as of 13.08.2018). Please check other consequences of part-time study (e.g. health insurance, child benefit, etc.) well in advance.

####

Since the winter semester 2013/14, tuition fees have no longer been charged in Bavaria. The basic fee for student services is currently 87 euros. This also applies to students on leave of absence, students on internships and students on semesters abroad.

####

No, the semester fee must be paid each semester.

### Change

####

title: More flexible part-time studying (2/2)
content:
More flexible part-time studying
Section: Studies Study offers Forms of study

A change from full-time to part-time and vice versa is possible once, after a discussion with study counselling, provided that a place is available in the respective degree program. Prior to this, a discussion with the study counselling must be held in which the reasons for a change are discussed and documented for the examination board. A further change is also only possible upon application. Proof must be provided that the reason for the first change no longer exists. It is not possible to switch to the other study model in the event of de-registration due to a failed full-time or part-time examination!

####

For students who were once enrolled on a full-time degree course, all examination deadlines continue to run as they did on the full-time degree course. Switching to a part-time degree course does not extend these deadlines further.

In addition, the change should only be made after a personal consultation. Here you will discuss with the student advisor whether a change (still) makes sense and how to proceed. After thorough examination and planning, submit an application for transfer to the Student office. You must also submit an online application for a higher semester. Please note the following deadlines: Beginning of May to July 15 for a transfer to the winter semester and mid-November to January 15 for a transfer to the summer semester.

### Crediting of previously completed examinations

####

Yes, all credits earned on the full-time course will be credited to the part-time course and vice versa. Please complete the application for credit transfer. Please note, however, that all (repeat) deadlines will also be taken into account.

####

In principle, every examination achievement must be checked by the module supervisor. The module supervisor will decide whether the work completed so far can be credited. To do this, you must also complete an application for credit transfer and submit it to the Examinations Office.

####

This depends on the degree programme you choose. If this requires a (pre)-internship, you must complete this in accordance with the requirements of the study and examination regulations.

####

Competences acquired outside of the university sector may not replace more than half of the competences to be proven. The Chair of the Examination Board decides on the comparability and creditability of achievements and skills acquired outside of the higher education sector.

### Requirements

####

The same admission requirements apply for the part-time course as for the full-time version. There is no NC, but a university entrance qualification recognized in Bavaria is required.

Professionally qualified students can also apply for a place on the course. Information on application and admission can be found on our website .

### Application

####

No, you can only apply for part-time or full-time study. If you apply for both types of study, only the application for full-time study will be considered. However, you can withdraw an application up to the end of the application period and submit a new one for the other type of study.

####

### Miscellaneous

####

No, in principle you can do any job alongside your studies. The important thing is that you have a flexible job so that you can adapt your working hours to the lecture times as soon as the course catalogues are online.

####

No, ECTS points are valid ‘for life’.

title: Motorsport Engineering
content:
Motorsport Engineering
Section: Studies Study offers Study programmes

## Everything at a glance

Degree level:
Bachelor of Engineering
(B.Eng.)

Standard period of study
: 7 Semester
(210 ECTS )

Type Of Study:

Full-time,
Dual

Study location:
Amberg

Start Of Study:

Winter- and summer semester (1. and higher semester)

Course Language:

German

The Motorsport Engineering programme offers a solid basic education in mechanical engineering complemented by specialist knowledge and forward-looking key technologies such as e-mobility, control engineering and lightweight construction. This combination, together with a strong practical orientation, ensures a wide range of possible applications - not only in the field of racing. Various electives integrated into the course allow for further specialisation in areas of individual interest.

Degree: BEng

Duration: 3 years

Start of studies: winter (October 1) and summer (March 15)

Application period: May 1 through July 15 for the winter term, November 20 through January 15 for the summer term

Admission Requirements:

General entrance qualification for admission to a university or technical college or a subject-related university entrance qualification. Admission is also possible via professional university access. Students have to serve a pre-study internship of at least twelve weeks in a relevant professional field prior to their studies or by the end of the third semester at the latest.

German B2 (language of instruction: German)

Course Content:

The programme comprises five different module groups.The module group Engineering Fundaments contains specialist modules from the area of mechanical engineering and vehicle techology:

- Technical Mechanics
- Materials Science and Chemistry
- Strength of Materials
- Engineering Design and 3D-CAD
- Electrical Engineering
- Machine Dynamics
- Technical Thermodynamics
- Heat and Mass Transfer
- Technical Fluid Mechanics
- Control Engineering

The module group Engineering Applications contains the following modules:

- Construction Elements
- Manufacturing Technology
- Strength of Materials and FEM
- Materials Science
- Electrical Drive Technology
- Measurement Technology
- Technical Product Development and Plastic-Compatible Design

The module group Practical Experience and Key Competencies involves course contents related to practical education.

- Internships
- Practical Semester

The module group Mathematics and Sciences involves the following modules:

- Mathematics
- Physics
- Computer Science
- Electrochemistry

The fifth module group involves specialist knowledge related to motorsport:

- Data Analysis in Motorsports
- Suspension Design and Multibody Simulation
- Rules and Regulations in Motorsports
- Motorsports-Specific Projects
- Elective Modules

For further information (in German), please switch to the German website.

## 5G4Healthcare

5G4Healthcare is one of the six research projects funded in the context of the 5G Innovation Programme of the Federal Ministry of Transport and Digital Infrastructure.

The goal of the 5G4Healthcare project, funded by the German Federal Ministry of Transport and Digital Infrastructure, is to explore the feasibility, opportunities, and limitations of improving the effectiveness and efficiency of rural healthcare through 5G technology and to derive recommendations for scalable solutions. Under the leadership of OTH Amberg-Weiden, the use of 5G in healthcare is being designed (Phase 1), implemented as a model (Phase 2), tested and evaluated (Phase 3). In this context, the new mobile communications standard 5G forms the basis for innovative medical care and services such as real-time ECG transmission from ambulances, robot-assisted operations, and remote monitoring and analysis of patients' vital data. The results of the project will be used to develop new solutions that will serve as a blueprint for a consistent digital health-based medical care approach in rural regions.

### DIGITAL BUSINESS - MAKE MORE OUT OF THE MARKET, PEOPLE AND MACHINES!

Designing customer experiences, making data-driven decisions, rethinking digital processes - on the Digital Business degree programme at OTH Amberg-Weiden, you will specialise directly in what really interests you. Three degree programmes, one goal : your future in the digital economy.

E-Commerce & Retail Management
You will learn how modern retail works - cross-channel, customer-centric and data-based. From online shop logic and customer journeys to strategic management in digital sales.

Analytics & data management
You turn data into strategic decisions. You analyse, visualise, interpret - and use methods and tools such as SPSS, SAP or BI software in a targeted manner.

Innovation & Process Management
You develop new business models and think digitally about processes. Whether agile project management, innovation methods or digital transformation - here you will become a shaper of change.

All degree programmes combine business thinking with digital know-how, practice with theory - and give you the tools you need for your path into companies, start-ups or self-employment. You will work on real projects, in small groups, with personal support. And you will not only become professionally fit - but also communicative, entrepreneurial and future-ready.

## Career prospects

With your degree in Digital Business, many doors are open to you - in commerce, industry, IT or consulting. Depending on which degree programme you choose, you can work as a:

- Marketing manager with a focus on digital customer experiences
- Management consultant for digital strategies
- Data analytics manager who enables data-based decisions
- Digital analytics expert in interaction with development, production and marketing
- Project manager in the digital transformation
- E-commerce specialist who develops and manages web shops
- Process manager for the optimisation of processes and workflows

Want even more? Then you can follow on directly with a suitable Master's degree - for example in Digital Business , Digital Entrepreneurship or one of our other future-oriented programmes.

Or you can go your own way: many of our graduates have successfully founded their own companies - with digital business models that they developed during their studies. We support you with expertise, workshops and personalised advice.

## HIGHLIGHTS of the course

Instead of just talking about digitalisation, you will develop your own solutions for real challenges in retail, industry and IT on the Digital Business degree programme. You will work in small teams on projects with practice partners, design digital business models or analyse data for strategic decisions. The results? Are often implemented directly in the company. Instead of dry theory, you use modern tools - from SAP and SPSS to business intelligence software. You will train your entrepreneurial thinking as well as your analysis and communication skills . You will benefit from personal support, interactive teaching formats and a study environment designed for digital collaboration.

What makes the degree programme special is that you choose one of three future-oriented study programmes from the outset - E-Commerce & Retail Management, Analytics & Data Management or Innovation & Process Management. This allows you to tailor your degree programme to your interests - and make you an expert in the digital economy.

## Certification Programmes

In addition to your regular studies, you can take certification courses at OTH Amberg-Weiden free of charge - for example in the areas of project management or digitalisation. These additional qualifications are a real plus for your CV and help you to position yourself specifically in your professional field. You can find an overview of all certificates here:

Certifications

## Structure

On the Bachelor's degree programme in Digital Business, you will learn everything you need to understand digital business models, use data intelligently and strategically design innovation processes. You will combine business thinking with digital expertise - and become a sought-after specialist for the digital economy.

You will attend courses on business fundamentals and key digital topics such as e-commerce, data analytics, process management and digital transformation. You will also develop personal skills in areas such as communication, teamwork and self-management - and regularly work on real projects with companies.

From the fourth semester onwards, you choose one of three specialised study programmes . You can choose from these:

- Analytics & Data Management
- E-Commerce & Retail Management
- Innovation & Process Management

In the sixth semester, you will apply your knowledge directly in a company during a practical semester lasting at least 18 weeks. And in the seventh semester, you will write your Bachelor's thesis - ideally on a specific practical issue.

# About us

The "Center of Excellence for Cogeneration Technologies" (CeCoGen) bundles the research activities of the Tech. Univ. of Applied Sciences Amberg-Weiden in the field of CHP technologies. It is affiliated with the Faculty of Mechanical Engineering / Environmental Technology and is funded by the Free State of Bavaria. The research focus of the CeCoGen is on optimising efficiency and reducing emissions in CHP, the use of new energy sources in CHP processes, sector coupling and systemic integration of CHP plants in energy supply structures and the development of new innovative CHP concepts.

title: Research
content:
Research
Section: Research Research environment Competence Centres

# Research

## Fields of Research

####

## Emission analysis and emission reduction

[Image: Two people carry out a HF-A emissions exhaust measurement]

In the field of cogeneration, a variety of different fuels are used, such as natural gas, biogas, biogenic liquid fuels, products from the thermochemical gasification of biomass with different qualities or even synthetic fuels such as hydrogen (H 2 ).

Particularly when new types of fuels are used, the exhaust emission behaviour has not yet been fully researched. In order to reduce emissions, the entire CHP process is being considered and optimised, from the fuel to the internal engine processes to the exhaust gas aftertreatment.

####

## Efficiency increase

[Image: 3D graphic illustrating the functioning of a microexpansion machine]

The overall objective of the research work is to increase the electrical and thermal efficiency of CHP systems through:

- Internal engine improvements
- Optimisation of peripheral components
- Waste heat conversion
- Micro-CHP

####

## Biogenic fuels

[Image: HF-C test stand wood gasifier]

The use of biogenic fuels as fuel for CHP systems is being investigated as part of this field of action.

- Adaptation and further development of combustion engines for use with biogenic fuels
- Ignition jet technology
- Hot air turbine processes for biomass CHP plants

####

## CHP system technology

[Image: Photo of the system technology in a CHP system]

The increasingly decentralised provision of energy requires the further development of the CHP system as a whole. This includes:

- Networking of CHP plants for the intelligent provision of electricity and heat
- Integration of storage technologies into CHP systems to balance out fluctuating electricity and heat demand.
- Provision of control energy to stabilise the grid in view of the increasing use of renewable energies.

####

## Innovative methods of CHP

[Image: Ignition jet CHP]

Of particular interest for application-oriented research are innovative and forward-looking technologies, such as:

- Use of fuel cells in the area of combined heat and power generation
- Micro-expansion turbines for CHP processes and micro-steam processes based on organic fluids (Organic Rankine Cycle)

## Projects

####

## Current projects

- CH2P
- eQBooster
- HyBaBo

####

## Completed projects

- Optibiosy
- Efficool
- Hocheffiziente Kraft-Wärme-Kopplung für Industrie und Gewerbe
- MOVE
- EUKI
- Flexeco2

title: Fields of expertise
content:
Fields of expertise
Section: Research Research environment Competence Centres

# Fields of expertise

####

## Test benches for CHP plants/ Technical Centre

[Image: Test stand for a combined heat and power unit]

- In the Technical Centre , 4 test benches are available for CHP units with an electrical output of up to 25 kW and 2 test benches for CHP units with an electrical output of up to 600 kW
- Test bench up to 240 kWel (dual-fuel CHP with 240 kWel)
- Dynamic engine test bench up to 240 kW (Siemens)
- Test bench for small engines up to 30 kW
- Mobile indexing systems (AVL Indimicro, Kistler, IMES) for combustion analysis
- Flow bench for flow measurements on cylinder heads
- Injection system test bench for injection rate and injection quantity (IAV Injection Analyzer)
- Measurement and control technology for real-time applications
- Various software tools for combustion analysis and simulation

####

## Emission measurement technology

[Image: Measuring device for emission measurement]

- Multicomponent emission analysis by means of FTIR spectroscopy (Gasmet / Ansyco) and conventional exhaust gas analysers (NDIR, CLD, FID, PMD)
- Mobile FTIR system (Gasmet / Ansyco)
- Portable exhaust gas analysis systems for industrial engines (Testo 350)
- Particle analysis using SMPS (TSI Scanning-Mobility-Particle-Sizer) and mobile particle counter (MS4 Pegasor)
- Gravimetric particle determination according to VDI 2066
- Conditioned weighing laboratory with microbalance (Mettler Toledo, resolution 1 µg)

####

## Mobile measurement technology

- Electrical energy and network analysers (Gossen Metrawatt, Hioki)
- Heat quantity measurement using clamp-on ultrasonic measurement technology (Flexim Fluxus)
- Thermography (Jenoptik Variocam, Fluke)
- Portable oscilloscopes for measurements on injection and ignition systems (Fluke 125)
- Temperature, pressure and flow measurement technology for ventilation and exhaust systems
- Mobile micro GC (Gasmet) for fuel gas analysis

####

## Software/ CAE tools

[Image: CAE of a computer cluster]

- Combustion and charge cycle analysis with AVL Indicom and AVL Concerto (incl. Burn/ GCA)
- Simulation Internal Combustion Engine (ICE) AVL Fire
- Fluid dynamic calculations with Ansys Workbench and Star CCM+
- Simulation of turbomachinery with Numeca FINE/Turbo
- Simulation of combustion engines with GT Power / GT Suite
- 3D design and calculation with PTC Creo, Catia V5 and MDESIGN
- Multi-body simulation with Adams
- Development of measurement and control systems with National Instruments LabVIEW

####

## Laboratory Energy Self-Sufficient Buildings

[Image: The construction of energy-autonomous buildings, illustrated by a circuit diagram]

- Stirling CHP 1 kWel, 5.8 kWth, 18 kWth Peak load burner
- Mini-BHKW 5 kWel, 12 kWth
- Photovoltaic system 7.65 kWp in east-west orientation
- 3-phase stand-alone inverter 8,000 VA
- Small wind turbines 1 kWel and 4 kWel
- Solar thermal system (flat-plate collector 6 m² and vacuum tubes 5.7 m²)
- 3 x electronic load max. 3,600 VA, heating cartridge 4.5 kWel
- 2 x air heater 26 kWth
- Lithium iron phosphate battery storage 15.6 kWhel
- 1,000 l stratified storage tank with 50 l domestic hot water tank

General Information:

This degree programme is about the sustainable use of energy and the utilization of energy sources that are replenished as they are used, such as wind, water, the sun and sustainably grown crops. This type of energy is almost inexhaustible and far more efficient than fossil fuels, guaranteeing climate protection and the preservation of natural resources. The programme provides the know-how required to develop and optimise environmentally friendly technologies for the generations of tomorrow. Given the importance of environmentally friendly technologies in virtually any field of industry, graduates enjoy excellent career prospects and a high employability rate.

Degree: BEng

Duration: 3 years

Start of studies: winter (October 1) and summer (March 15)

Application period: May 1 through July 15 for the winter term, November 20 through January 15 for the summer term

Entrance requirements:

General entrance qualification for admission to a university or technical college or a subject-related university entrance qualification. Admission is also possible via professional university access. Students have to serve a pre-study internship of at least twelve weeks in a relevant professional field prior to their studies or by the end of the third semester at the latest.

German B2 (language of instruction: German)

Contents and Structure:

The programme consists of three module groups.

The first module group provides the mathematical and scientific fundamentals :

- Mathematics
- Physics
- Basics of Chemistry and Biology
- Materials Science
- Technical Mechanics and Design
- Electrical Engineering and Information Technology

The second group - fundamentals of science and engineering – includes the following modules:

- Thermodynamics and Fluid Mechanics
- Process Engineering
- Heat Transfer and Reaction Kinetics
- Biotechnology
- Physical Chemistry
- Control Engineering
- Measurement and Sensor Technology
- Electronics and Digital Technology

The third module group includes engineering-related content , such as

- Electrical Power Engineering
- Energy Conversion in Engines and Machines
- Combustion Engine Technology for Renewable Fuels
- Efficient Energy Utilisation
- Decentralised Energy Systems
- Energy Conversion Systems
- Fuel Cell Technology
- Integrated Energy Concepts

- Basics of Energy Technology and Energy Management
- Solar Energy
- Wind and Hydro Power
- Energy Efficiency of Buildings

Interdisciplinary Modules:

- Business and Management
- Environmental and Energy Law

The last semester is designated for the completion of the final research paper (Bachelor’s Thesis) which may also cover research carried out in connection with practical placement at a company.

For further information (in German), please switch to the German website.

# Certificates

# Academic modules

The certificate modules at OTH Amberg Weiden integrate academic study with practical professional experience, combining interdisciplinary and specialized expertise with strong methodological and interpersonal skills to support your future success.

Our practice-oriented modules in the fields of digitalization, business, law, engineering, and health offer you the opportunity to pursue targeted and individualized continuing education. Advance your qualifications with our part-time modules to meet the growing demands of the professional world and benefit from our flexible modular system.

## Flexible modular system

With our modules (from basic to advanced), you make a visible investment in your professional development. You not only acquire essential foundational knowledge but also deepen your expertise in selected subject areas. Here’s how it works:

- If you successfully complete a module and pass the examination, you will earn up to 5 ECTS credits (European Credit Transfer and Accumulation System).
- If you combine three modules worth 5 ECTS each according to your individual preferences and successfully complete the examinations, you will receive a certificate totaling 15 ECTS credits.
- If you add three additional modules worth 5 ECTS each to these three modules and successfully complete the examination, you will obtain an advanced certificate totaling 30 ECTS credits.

# Work-study program

A Work-study degree program allows you to earn a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree flexibly without interrupting your career. Benefit from practical, career-focused content, modern learning formats like blended learning , and an optimal balance between work and study. Boost your career prospects with a professional continuing education program designed to meet current job market demands.

A Work-study degree program or continuing education course is specifically designed to be completed alongside full-time employment. This means there is no need to leave your job or risk a career setback due to a difficult re-entry into the workforce. You can continue earning an income while working toward a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree—with only a few vacation days required each year.

Many employers already take advantage of the OTH Professional continuing education program and its certificates to support staff development.

For employers, Work-study programs offer an ideal way to further qualify employees and future leaders without disrupting day-to-day business operations. Like traditional full-time programs, these courses are generally designed as on-campus programs, allowing participants to benefit from direct interaction with professors and lecturers. However, classes are scheduled in the evenings, on weekends, and in block formats, incorporating modern teaching methods such as blended learning and virtual learning environments.

OTH Amberg-Weiden offers one part-time Bachelor’s program and several part-time Master’s programs within its OTH Professional continuing education portfolio.

Consider discussing this opportunity with your manager, or contact us directly—we are happy to liaise with your HR department if needed.

#### Bachelor’s program

Our flexible program enables working professionals to pursue a university degree at their own pace. The curriculum is practical, career-focused, and tailored to real-world professional needs. This allows you to effectively combine career advancement with higher education.

#### Master´s program

Our customized part-time Master’s programs are designed for working professionals seeking academic advancement. Flexible class schedules make it easy to balance your career, studies, and personal life.

# Partners

## Our partners

In addition to the expertise of OTH Amberg-Weiden, OTH Professional builds on strong regional and international partnerships with companies and educational providers. Through our continuing education programs, you benefit from the expertise of experienced lecturers and can actively shape your professional development in a focused and goal-oriented way.
Below, we introduce some of our partners.

### Steuerlehrgänge Dr. Bannas

OTH Professional cooperates with Steuerlehrgänge Dr. Bannas GmbH in the Master’s program in Tax Law and Taxation (LL.M.) . Steuerlehrgänge Dr. Bannas GmbH offers training for tax advisor qualification as well as courses for becoming a certified tax specialist (Steuerfachwirt) ( www.steuerlehrgaenge.com (http://www.steuerlehrgaenge.com) ).

The postgraduate Master’s program via OTH Professional enables professionals who have already completed a university degree in Business Administration or Law to qualify for demanding specialist and leadership roles in corporate taxation within an increasingly globalized environment. In addition, the program prepares students for the professional tax advisor examination. You can also find more information about the program at Steuerlehrgänge Dr. Bannas GmbH (https://www.master-steuerrecht-weiden.de/frankfurt-amweiden.html) and on our website under Master’s program .

### ARBER-Seminare GmbH

OTH Professional cooperates with ARBER Seminare in the field of academic and research-oriented continuing education within Master’s programs (LL.M.). Since 1997, ARBER Seminare have supported and guided lawyers across Germany in obtaining additional qualifications as specialist attorneys through high-quality specialist legal training courses. These programs provide the foundation for the award of the specialist lawyer title by the respective regional bar associations. In addition, continuing education courses in accordance with Section 15 of the German Specialist Lawyers’ Regulations (FAO) are offered. Further information on the degree programs can be found at ARBER Campus (https://www.arber-campus.de/) and Master´s program .

### AK Jura

OTH Professional cooperates with AK Jura and offers innovative Master’s programs (LL.M.) in the field of academic and research-oriented continuing education.

AK Jura supports lawyers in obtaining additional qualifications as specialist attorneys through high-quality training programs. These courses prepare participants for the specialist lawyer title awarded by the regional bar associations.

Further information can be found at AK Jura (http://www.ak-jura.de/) and Master´s program .

### 121WATT - School for Digital Marketing & Innovation

"We share knowledge!" is the motto of our cooperation partner 121WATT (https://www.121watt.de/weiterbildung/mba-digital-marketing/) - School for Digital Marketing & Innovation. Comparable to the reform pedagogical principle “Help me to do it myself,” the motto of 121Watt also reflects the idea of how teaching and learning can be meaningfully designed. Participants in continuing education programs should be optimally prepared for current challenges, such as those arising from ongoing digitalization. Instructors teach and share their expertise in a practice- and experience-oriented way, openly and without reservation. The goal is to enable participants to become fully capable of acting independently and to engage with colleagues and stakeholders on an equal professional level.

Learn from experienced top-level practitioners how to effectively apply online marketing, SEO, Google Ads, Facebook, and Google Analytics in your organization.

### Fraunhofer Academy

The Fraunhofer Institute for Applied and Integrated Security and OTH Amberg Weiden offer high-quality training courses in cybersecurity and the development of IT security skills for specialists and managers at the Learning Lab Weiden. Current scientific and research findings on topics such as embedded systems, mobile security, and the Internet of Things are translated into practice-oriented training programs. The Learning Lab in Weiden is one of the few research facilities in the field of IT security in northern Bavaria and provides a modern lab environment directly on the university campus. Clients from all industries benefit from tailored and needs-based training courses and seminars.

Within the Cybersecurity Learning Lab, Fraunhofer (https://www.academy.fraunhofer.de/de/weiterbildung.html) and OTH Amberg-Weiden offer compact, transfer-oriented training formats for on the job professional qualification.

In flexibly combinable modules and tailored to different professional roles, real-world threat scenarios are simulated and appropriate solution concepts are developed in a practice-oriented way.

Data processing

This privacy policy applies to the web application of the BigBlueButton web conferencing service of the Ostbayerische Technische Hochschule Amberg-Weiden at "https://bbb.oth-aw.de" and to the personal and non-personal data collected therein.

The purpose of the BigBlueButton web conferencing service of the OTH Amberg-Weiden is digital collaboration within the scope of official activities at the OTH Amberg-Weiden, in particular ensuring cross-spatial teaching, research and administration, in the sense of the legal task of cultivating and developing the sciences and arts (Art. 2 BayHSchG), the compatibility of family with studies, science and career Art. 2 Para. 3 BayHSchG) and the promotion of international and European cooperation in higher education Art. 2 Para. 4 BayHSchG) in accordance with the applicable Bavarian Higher Education Act.

The processing of personal data in the context of the use of the BigBlueButton web conferencing service is based on the following legal bases:

Consent according to Art. 6 Para. 1 a) DSGVO

For the fulfilment of official duties pursuant to Art. 6 Para. 1 e) DSGVO in connection with Art. 4 BayDSG. Art. 4 BayDSG in conjunction with. Art 2 BayHSchG
For data processing in the context of contractual relationships Art. 6 para. 1 b) DSGVO

Personal data

According to Article 4 GDPR, "personal data means any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person [...]; an identifiable natural person is one who can be identified, directly or indirectly, in particular by reference to an identifier such as a name, an identification number, location data, an online identifier or to one or more factors specific to the physical, physiological, genetic, mental, economic, cultural or social identity of that natural person".

Data for the technical delivery of the website

For the delivery of the website by the web application to the user's computer or web browser, a temporary processing of the complete IP address by the web server and the downstream web applications is necessary for technical reasons.

The collection, processing and transfer of personal data of users from the public is carried out on the basis of this data protection declaration and, if required, with the express consent of the users.

content:
Privacy Policy for the BigBlueButton Web Conferencing Service
Section: Legal Data Privacy

Place of processing and storage

The data processed in the web application are not processed and stored outside the scope of the GDPR.

Cookies

A so-called cookie is a text fragment that the website places on the computer of the requesting party via the web browser and whose content is transmitted to the website again each time the web browser accesses the website.

For purposes limited purely to the functionality of the web application, temporary session and authorisation cookies are set that do not allow cross-application identification of the user. This includes the following purposes in particular:

- Authentication of the user's current web session against the web application
- Authentication of the current web session of the user's central identity provider against the web application.
- Storage for application-specific settings, e.g. language selected by the user, session runtime.

Tracking cookies are set for purposes beyond the pure functionality of the application. This includes in particular the following purposes:

- Creation of anonymised website access statistics via the central website statistics service of the OTH Amberg-Weiden to improve the web application and the web content offered. Further information can be found in the section "Evaluations".

The storage of cookies can be deactivated in the web browser used by the user. In this case, no cookies are stored. As a result, however, no personal functions of the website can be executed.

Evaluations

In order to improve the web application and the web content offered, anonymised website access statistics are created via the central website statistics service of the OTH Amberg-Weiden.

You have the option of completely deactivating the evaluations carried out via the central website statistics service of the OTH Amberg-Weiden (opt-out). This can be done by one of the following measures:

- By deactivating tracking in the tracking settings of the OTH Amberg-Weiden.
- By activating the so-called "Do Not Track signalling" in the settings of the web browser (applies to all websites)
- By deactivating cookies in the web browser settings (not recommended, as this makes the web application no longer usable in a meaningful way).

Logged data in the web server

When you access the website, the following personal data is stored in the form of access logs of the web server:

- IP address
- Access date/time
- Access method
- Access success
- accessed resource
- Volume of data transferred
- Web browser designation

In the access logs created by the web server, the IP address of the user is processed and stored for a period of 7 full days to defend against attacks, prevent misuse, analyse errors and improve the web application.

Logged data in the web application

When you access the website, the following data is stored in the form of web application access logs:

- IP address
- access date/time
- Action performed and resource accessed
- Session or authorisation ID
- User ID
- Your name
- Your email address
- Room

In the access logs created by the web application, the IP address of the users is processed and stored for a period of 7 full days to defend against attacks, prevent misuse, analyse errors and improve the web application.

Links to websites of other providers

The websites may contain links to websites of other providers. The OTH Amberg-Weiden has no influence on whether these providers also comply with the legal data protection regulations. Please always check the data protection declarations of the other providers.

Recipients of your data in case of legal or judicial obligation

Apart from being passed on to authorised service providers, the data stored when you access the website will only be passed on to third parties if we are obliged to do so by law or by a court decision or if this is necessary for legal or criminal prosecution in the event of an attack on the website.

Your rights

As a user of the website, you have various rights in accordance with Articles 15 to 18, 21 DSGVO and the BayDSG: right to information, right to rectification, right to deletion, right to restriction of processing, right to object and right to lodge a complaint.

If the processing of your data is based on consent, you have the right to revoke this consent at any time with effect for the future.

Right of access

According to Article 15 of the GDPR, you can request information about your personal data that we process. In your request for information, you should specify your request in order to make it easier for us to compile the necessary data. Please note that your right to information is restricted by Section 34 of the BDSG or Article 10 of the BayDSG.

Right of deletion

In accordance with Article 17 DSGVO and Section 35 BDSG, you can request the deletion of your personal data. Your right to erasure depends on a number of conditions, such as whether we still need your data to fulfil our legal duties.

Right of objection

Under Article 21 of the GDPR, you have the right to object at any time, on grounds relating to your particular situation, to the processing of data concerning you. However, we cannot always comply with your objection, for example if a legal provision obliges us to process in accordance with Section 36 BDSG. Please also note that it is mandatory for us to process the IP address of your client so that you can use the website.

Right of complaint

If you are of the opinion that OTH Amberg-Weiden has not complied with data protection regulations when processing your data, you can lodge a complaint with the official data protection officer of OTH Amberg-Weiden or with the supervisory authority for public bodies processing data in the Free State of Bavaria in order to have it examined.

[Translate to Englisch:] Mit Ablauf des 30.09.2023 tritt die Rahmenprüfungsordnung für die Fachhochschulen außer Kraft.


Gemäß § 9 Abs. 4 der Hochschulprüferverordnung (HSchPrüferV) gilt folgendes:

Studierende, die ihr Studium an einer staatlichen Hochschule für angewandte Wissenschaften in einem Studiengang mit Abschluss Bachelor oder Master vor dem Wintersemester 2023/2024 aufgenommen haben, schließen ihr Studium auf der Grundlage der Vorschriften des § 4 Abs. 2 und 3 der RaPO für die Fachhochschulen in der am 30.09.2023 geltenden Fassung sowie der §§ 5, 7 bis 11 der RaPO für die Fachhochschulen in der am 30.09.2023 geltenden Fassung ab.


https://www.gesetze-bayern.de/Content/Document/BayHSchPrueferV-9


Relevante Regelungen der RaPO wurden in die neu beschlossene ASPO (Allgemeine Studien- und Prüfungsordnung) welche für Studierende ab dem Wintersemester 2023/2024 gilt, aufgenommen.

## Everything at a glance

Degree level:
Master of Engineering
(M.Eng.)

Standard period of study
: 3 Semester
(90 ECTS )

Type Of Study:

Full-time,
Part-time,
Dual

Study location:
Weiden

Start Of Study:

Winter semester (1. semester) and summer semester (1. semester)

Course Language:

German

The interdisciplinary master's program in Industrial Engineering - Digital Engineering & Management focuses on a current and future megatrend: the digitalization of operational processes in terms of the advancement of „Industry 4.0”. You will learn about technological and methodological approaches to integrating processes and components into the value chain through digitalized information flows to achieve higher efficiency. In addition to teaching the technical fundamentals, we also strive to make learning tangible, for example by using of state-of-the-art laboratory equipment and by including practical operational examples as well as business games and project work.

This program does not require a previous degree in Computer Science. Instead, as a consecutive course, it is primarily designed for graduates of a bachelor's program in Industrial Engineering or similar bachelor's programs with a mix of technical and business content . In the case of a purely technical pre-study, such as mechanical engineering, additional business (40 ECTS) and integrative (20 ECTS) qualifications must be proven or there must be a willingness to catch up on these in parallel with the master's program.

Upon successful completion of the program, you will be awarded the academic degree "Master of Engineering (M.Eng.)".

By choosing this degree program, you will be well-equipped for optimizing the operational value chain through digitalization approaches !

Further features of the program:

- There are two models of study, either full-time or part-time.
- 4 modules with a total of 20 out of 65 ECTS (excluding the final research paper) can be freely selected from a catalogue of defined courses
- planned group size: about 30 students
- systematic involvement of external specialists, for example from companies active in the field of digitalization

title: Information security (1/3)
content:
Information security
Section: University About our university Facilities

# Information security

Welcome to our information security page.

## General Information

### The definitions of terms are taken from the glossary of the German Federal Office for Information Security (BSI).

####

Information security aims to protect information. Information can be stored on paper, in computers or in people's heads. The protection goals or basic values of information security are confidentiality, integrity and availability.

Confidentiality is the protection against unauthorized disclosure of information. Confidential data and information must only be accessible to authorized persons in the permitted manner.

Integrity refers to ensuring the correctness (integrity) of data and the proper functioning of systems. When the term integrity is applied to "data," it expresses that the data is complete and unchanged. In information technology, however, it is usually defined more broadly and applied to "information." In this context, the term "information" is used to refer to "data" that can be assigned certain attributes, such as author or time of creation, depending on the context. The loss of integrity of information can therefore mean that it has been altered without authorization, that details of the author have been falsified, or that the time at which it was created has been manipulated.

The availability of services, functions of an IT system, IT applications or IT networks, or even of information, exists if they can always be used by users as intended.

####

Information technology (IT) includes all technical means that serve to process or transmit information. Information processing includes the collection, recording, use, storage, transmission, program-controlled processing, internal presentation and output of information.

Accordingly, IT security must protect all technical means that serve to process or transmit information. It thus represents a subarea of information security.

####

Data protection is intended to protect individuals from having their personal rights impaired by the handling of their personal data. Data protection therefore refers to the protection of personal data against possible misuse by third parties. Suitable technical and organizational measures (TOMs) must be taken for this purpose.

While data protection aims to protect personal data, information security is concerned with maintaining the protection of information, data and systems.

Strict legal regulations apply in data protection.

## Threats

### What are the threats to IT security? The consequences of these threats can lead to IT failure, data loss, leakage/manipulation of personal/secret data, identity theft, among others.

####

Phishing is a combination of the words "password" and "fishing". Phishing is an attempt to obtain access data for a service or website, for example, by means of fake E-mails or websites. Under certain circumstances (see social engineering), the victim does not question or recognize the actual authenticity of such a message or website and then unwittingly gives his or her access data into unauthorized hands.

Vishing (voice phishing) is a form of fraud via telephone. The scammers use manipulative tactics, for example, posing as employees of other Universities, business partners, friends or relatives, in order to gain access to their victims' sensitive data.

Quishing (phishing with QR codes) are phishing emails that contain a QR code instead of a link, which in turn tempts the user to enter their access data or is used to download malicious code. Unlike links and attachments, QR codes are viewed as images by current anti-virus programs and are therefore generally classified as harmless. This makes it more likely that such emails will be delivered directly to the users' mailboxes. The user is asked to take urgent action by scanning the QR code with his smartphone, which in turn leads to a manipulated website.

Smishing (phishing via SMS) is a form of fraud via (mobile) SMS with malicious links. Malware is then either installed on the device via this link or you are asked to enter personal data such as passwords, account data, etc. on a fake page that is not recognizable as such.

####

Social engineering exploits human characteristics such as curiosity, helpfulness, trust, fear, or respect for authority to skillfully manipulate people. In this way, cyber criminals entice the victim, for example, to disclose confidential information, bypass security functions, make bank transfers, or install malware on the end device at home or on the company network. Such social engineering attacks can take the form of a conversation, by phone, by e-mail or on social media.

CEO fraud as a special form of social engineering:

Here, perpetrators try to manipulate people in the company who are authorized to make decisions so that they transfer large sums of money abroad. The perpetrators pretend that the order comes directly from the head of the company (managing director or board member = chief executive officer = CEO).

####

Malware are malicious programs designed to cause harm to the user.

They are often multifunctional and, once they have infected a system, can download additional malware from the Internet, which then causes further damage.

There are numerous subtypes of malware, e.g. viruses, worms, trojans, rootkits, botnets, ransomware, spyware ... All work differently and cause different damage.

Malware is spread via malicious email attachments, links, macros in Office documents, manipulated USB sticks, among others.

####

Vulnerabilities in products/services can be exploited by attackers to penetrate IT systems, tap data and/or execute malware.

Countermeasure: Regularly update IT products/applications!

The BSI regularly reports such vulnerabilities: https://www.bsi.bund.de/DE/Service-Navi/Abonnements/Newsletter/Buerger-CERT-Abos/Buerger-CERT-Sicherheitshinweise/buerger-cert-sicherheitshinweise_node.html (https://www.bsi.bund.de/DE/Service-Navi/Abonnements/Newsletter/Buerger-CERT-Abos/Buerger-CERT-Sicherheitshinweise/buerger-cert-sicherheitshinweise_node.html)

## Best Practice (students)

####

title: Information security (2/3)
content:
Information security
Section: University About our university Facilities

The following rules are based on the password policy at OTH-AW:

- The password for the University-wide OTH-AW identifier is known only to the University member.
- Under no circumstances may the password be given to third parties, not even to a good friend/fellow student.
- Please be sure to use a secure OTH-AW password : as long as possible (at least 10 characters) with upper and lower case letters, numbers and special characters; do not use last name, first name, user name; do not use words from dictionaries/encyclopedias; do not use personal information that is easy to find out.
- While entering the password via the keyboard, make sure that no third party is watching
- Under no circumstances should the OTH-AW password be used in private with other providers, e.g. with a private e-mail account/Internet service! If this is the case, please change the OTH-AW password!
- If the password is entered incorrectly more than three times, access will be automatically blocked for a certain period of time. Please contact the computer centre by phone.
- Please never share the password unencrypted by e-mail!
- Password change always via the ‘Password change’ (https://support.oth-aw.de/help/en-us/8-account-und-login/5-wie-andere-ich-mein-passwort) -Service.
- To keep the user ID+password combination assigned per application/service, it is recommended to use a password manager tool such as KeePass.
- If passwords are stored in the web browser (product dependency!), then it is essential to secure them with a secure master password (not the OTH-AW password!)!
- If passwords are stored in written form, make sure to store them securely (preferably in a safe!), i.e. inaccessible to others.

####

- To access your mails, use either the university's GroupWise client , WebMail (via Browser) or an alternative mail client .
- For access via smartphone use the smartphone data synchronization of the data center!
- Communication with the university should only be done via the OTH-AW mail address!
- If the sender's mail address is not @oth-aw.de, such mails are always marked with the subject line prefix [EXTERN]. This is to visually mark mails in which the name of an OTH-AW member (e.g. professor) is misused as sender, in order to support you in recognizing spam/phishing mails. Possibly ask by phone!
- Please do not forward OTH-AW mails to a private email address!
- Mails sent to the university from a private email address will not be processed!
- The OTH-AW mail address should not be used for private use (e.g. for private orders). It is imperative to use a private e-mail address with its own password for this purpose.
- Before opening a mail, please do the 3-second security check: Is the sender known? Does the subject make sense? Do you expect an attachment from this sender?
- After opening, doubts should arise in the following cases: impersonal salutation, request for personal information, building up time pressure, threats, promises to win, etc.
- Delete such unwanted mails (SPAM or PHISHING) immediately and do not react to them in any way! So do not reply, do not open links, do not open attachments, do not call, do not buy anything!
- You can report such mails by forwarding the mail AS ANNEX to spam@oth-aw.de or phishing@oth-aw.de .

####

- When working in PC pools, be sure to use your personal area on the MyFiles Filr file server for data backup, which is regularly backed up by the computer center.
- Secure data exchange via the OTH-AW internal file server MyFiles Filr (= internal cloud) – also possible with non-university members.
- External clouds (= outside the university) should be used sparingly for university data exchange. Depending on the confidentiality level** , the data should be encrypted in advance (V3, V4) and also only stored there for as long as necessary.
- Gigamove is recommended as an external cloud for secure data exchange of very large files.
- External clouds from commercial providers (e.g. Dropbox) are not considered compliant with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). With such often free external clouds, you pay with your data. The OTH-AW access data (mail address, user ID, password) must not be used or deposited with external cloud providers as a matter of principle.
- Data from external clouds are not backed up by OTH-AW.
- The cloud guidelines in force at OTH-AW must be observed.

** Confidentiality levels:

V1 = public, V2 = internal, V3 = OTH-AW confidential, V4 = strictly confidential.

V1 examples: Course catalog, press releases, flyers, public events, public portions of website.

V2 examples: Intranet, process portal, rules and regulations, instructions for action, correspondence, internal e-mails, internal telephone directories, internal events

V3 examples: personal data, travel, payroll, research data, technical data, restricted theses, auditing

V4 examples: in cooperation with third parties (military, research, business) due to official or contractual obligation

####

- Secure connection to the OTH network via VPN-Access
- Video-conferencing via BigBlueButton, Jitsi
- Virtual courses/lectures: Moodle (https://moodle.oth-aw.de) , BBB via Moodle
- Communication/Chat: RocketChat (https://rocket.oth-aw.de)
- Team/project work: MicroFocus Vibe (https://vibe.oth-aw.de) , MyFiles Filr , MS Teams (with limitations)
- Polls/voting via scheduler (https://terminplaner.dfn.de/)

####

- If possible, only use https websites (s stands for secure, i.e. encrypted communication!).

- Before clicking on links or images, check the actual link by mouseover: Mouseover without clicking shows the actual web address (look closely at WER area between http(s):// and next /!).
- Software downloads only from trusted sites or official stores.
- Refrain from doing anything that disrupts or jeopardizes the proper operation of the University's facilities.

####

## Awareness strengthening

### Awareness strengthening offers opportunities to strengthen one's own information security awareness. This supports and improves information security in the university (and also privately!).

SecAware.nrw - a self-learning academy for more cyber and information security at universities.

This project was launched to provide students and researchers at the universities of Nordrhein-Westfalen with the necessary knowledge and security awareness. This learning offer sensitizes users and creates or strengthens the corresponding IT skills in the context of cyber attacks.

The focus is on a flexible and intuitive online learning offer that enables participants to develop themselves independently and at their own pace.
