## UAre@OTHAW - Scholarship Program for Refugees from Ukraine

The UAre@OTHAW project was realised at OTH Amberg-Weiden as part of the DAAD funding programme "Future Ukraine – Scholarship Programme for Refugees from Ukraine at German Universities".

The project was coordinated by KOMO (OTH AW Competence Centre Bavaria – Central and Eastern Europe). During the project period from January 2023 to July 2025 , a total of five Master's students and ten Bachelor's students received a monthly scholarship. This financial support enabled the recipients to continue their studies despite the difficult circumstances resulting from the Russian war of aggression.

The scholarship holders also benefited from individual support, language courses, coaching and access to new networks. This enabled them not only to expand their technical and language skills, but also to develop new perspectives for their personal and professional future .

OTH Amberg-Weiden remains committed to cooperation with Ukrainian universities and supports students and teachers in other projects , such as the DAAD funded project Tandem UA-DE .

The scholarship holders have embarked on impressive paths and given a lot back to the university through their commitment. Some of them have organised several information events for prospective students from Ukraine and continue to support them in their goal of studying in Germany.

content:
Project description
Section: International International profile MINTeGreat

# Project description

The MINTeGreat project is part of DAAD’s FIT programme “Campus Initiative for International Talents” and addresses international STEM students.

DAAD, along with funding from the Federal Ministry of Education and Research, supports German universities in preparing prospective international students for the challenges of studying in Germany, the integration into their professional studies, and the subsequent transition into the German job market.

The FIT programme promotes the buildup of measures for study preparation, academic support, and academic success for international students at German universities.

On April 1, 2024, the FIT programme launched with a total of 89 projects nationwide. The MINTeGreat project subdivides into 4 modules:

Study Preparation

International students can attend our German A1- B2 immersion courses before enrolling in their professional studies. From enrollment on, students will receive support with integration and the start of studies.

Academic Support

During the studies, subject-specific German language courses are offered (e. g. professional German language training or German for Engineers), as well as seminars and workshops about living and studying in Germany.

Employability

This module prepares students for the German job market.
Job application trainings, workshops on labour culture in German companies, and mentor programmes are offered.

Labour Market Integration

Finally, the last module is all about networking with potential employers. Networking events with partner companies promotes career entry.

MINTeGreat is funded by the German Academic Exchange Service (DAAD) as part of the FIT programme “Campus Initiative for International Talents”. The project started in 2024 and will continue until the end of 2028.

Vorlesung Prof. Dr. Jan Sauer

### Practical Project with BHS Intralogistics: New Approaches to Modern Recruiting

How can companies effectively attract and recruit highly qualified technical specialists and managers? Students from the Bachelor’s degree programme in Applied Business Psychology explored this question in collaboration with BHS Intralogistics GmbH . Under the supervision of Simone I. Orlowski, Ph.D. (LU, USA) , two project groups developed evidence-based recommendations for recruiting Senior SPS Engineers and Senior Electrical Engineers.

As part of the Leadership Psychology II module, the students worked through the entire research process – from developing the research question and designing questionnaires to collecting and analysing data and presenting their findings. The practice project demonstrates how the degree programme combines scientific methods with real-world business challenges , creating valuable benefits for both students and regional industry partners.

Read more

### Searching for applicants with AI?

‘Searching for applicants with AI?’ - is the title of a current research article by Prof. Dr. Jan Sauer and Prof. Dr. Christian Schieder, which deals with the use of artificial intelligence in personnel selection. Together with students, the two professors are investigating how AI can change the approach to applicants, pre-selection and decision-making processes in recruitment - and which opportunities, limitations and acceptance factors play a role in this.

They are not only analysing the potential of intelligent systems , but also taking a critical look at the legal and ethical framework - particularly with regard to SMEs and the European AI Act. The project is exemplary of the research-based teaching at OTH Amberg-Weiden: scientifically sound, socially relevant and closely linked to current developments in the world of work.

Further practical research and co-operation projects will follow.

"I decided to study applied business psychology because I have always been fascinated by economic relationships – but a traditional business administration degree seemed too theoretical to me. In today's working world, social skills are just as important as technical knowledge. This is exactly where this degree programme comes in: it combines economic fundamentals with psychological expertise and interpersonal skills. I found the practical specialisation modules particularly exciting, in which we worked on real projects and gained direct insights from experienced lecturers from the business world. This helped me to better understand the content and internalise it in the long term. If you want to learn how to design economic processes with psychological sensitivity while strengthening your personal skills, this degree programme is the right choice for you."

Alina Wimmer - Graduate

"AWP combined my interest in psychology with my desire for a career change into an exciting industry that was new to me. I was surprised that I was even able to gain something positive from the maths modules - every subject offers real added value in addition to the obvious things I learnt. There were challenges, of course, but even these helped rather than held me back. Discipline and belief in my own potential were crucial for me. My tip: if you're unsure, look for role models, be courageous - and then just do it."

"I originally come from a technical background, but had wanted to develop in the direction of business for some time. Business psychology was the perfect combination of economic thinking and psychological issues for me. This makes the degree programme much more varied than traditional business studies. I particularly like the wide range of modules, from HR and marketing to psychology and many other interesting areas. ## Digital Business Labs

### Digital Business Lab - Vom Sensor zum Geschäftsmodell

Experience practice - understand processes - use data intelligently

The practical application of digital business models plays a central role in the Digital Business degree programme. In the specially equipped Digital Business Lab at OTH Amberg-Weiden, real business processes are simulated on a small scale - so-called ‘use cases’ from the business world, which enable students to actively experience and analyse the interplay between technology, computer science and business administration.

One particular example is the coffee production demonstration process currently being developed: a complete, digitally monitored production process is being set up from the bean to the finished beverage. Sensors continuously record relevant process data at various stations - such as temperature, fill levels or throughput times.

This data is not only used for visualisation, but is also analysed, interpreted and processed for economic decisions as part of the course. The aim is to sensitise students to the intelligent use of data in operational processes - and to show them in a practical way how modern digital value creation works.

The lab is currently being expanded - and is constantly growing with new components, stations and application scenarios. It thus offers a lively learning and experimental space for interdisciplinary work at the interface of business and technology.

title: Insights into the Master's in Applied Business Psychology (1/2)
content:
Insights into the Master's in Applied Business Psychology
Section: Studies Study offers Study programmes

## Insights

## Einblicke in den Studienalltag

## Summer and Winter Schools

##

In February 2025, students from OTH Amberg-Weiden travelled to the University of Prishtina in Kosovo for the first time for the international Winter School on Leadership. Bachelor's and Master's students from a total of eight different degree programmes at both universities took part - including Applied Business Psychology and International Management & Sustainability.

The academic week focussed on topics such as personality development, leadership skills and intercultural communication. The participants analysed personality profiles, reflected with the JoHari window, simulated team and leadership roles and developed creative approaches to situational leadership using the LEGO® Serious Play® method.

Another highlight: the exchange about the Kosovan education system and the cultural diversity that is practised. A lively, interdisciplinary dialogue was created with students from seven nations - led by lecturers from both universities.

The Winter School was not only a professional success, but also the start of an intensive partnership with the University of Prishtina - with a view to future joint projects and exchange formats.

##

As part of the international collaboration with Istanbul University, Master's students from the Applied Business Psychology and International Management & Sustainability degree programmes travelled to the Turkish metropolis for a summer school in July 2022.

The aim of the one-week stay was to develop intercultural skills and exchange ideas on current topics in business psychology in an international context. In interactive mini-lectures and workshops, the participants explored psychological issues relating to leadership, collaboration and cultural differences.

Away from the seminar room, the accompanying cultural programme offered numerous impressions: Visiting the Camlica Mosque and the Hagia Sophia, having dinner together and talking to fellow Turkish students, the students experienced the country, people and way of life at first hand.

##

As part of OTH Amberg-Weiden's international cooperation with partners in Chile, students on the Master's degree programme in Applied Business Psychology travelled to Santiago des Chile in January 2020 as part of the Summer School.

The focus was on intercultural and professional exchange on current topics in the field of business psychology. The specialist focus was on working with personality profiles. The Chilean-German student groups determined the appropriate leadership style for each profile and worked out the effects between leadership models and the composition of co-operative teams as well as the development of employees. In reciprocal interviews, they practised job interviews and staff appraisals in English.

## Testimonials

"As an industrial engineer, it is my job to act as an interface between people with different educational backgrounds, characters and objectives. After ten years of professional experience, most recently managing executives, I realised how important people are for the economic success of a company. I therefore decided to study for a Master's degree in Applied Business Psychology at the OTH Amberg-Weiden in order to improve my practical management skills and gain a sound psychological insight into human behaviour in the business environment. In addition to the well-balanced and exciting module profile, a decisive reason that led me to this university was the noticeable closeness of the lecturers, staff and programme management and the noticeable flexibility for working people. In particular, the teaching of the complex psychological content with understandable and practical examples made it easier for me, with my engineering background, to fully follow the topics that were new to me. I feel the benefits of the degree programme most clearly in my job and am able to reach people even better, connect with each other and carry out projects efficiently thanks to the new skills I have learnt."
Benjamin Hammami - Student

"I'm just as interested in economic relationships as I am in human behaviour and psychological backgrounds. This degree programme is the perfect way to unite and combine both areas of interest. These aspects are becoming increasingly important in practice, as organisations are placing more emphasis on responding to their employees and creating a motivating working atmosphere for them. At OTH Amberg-Weiden, I appreciate not only the degree programme but also the fact that lecturers are always on hand to offer help and advice. The mix of students from the region, Germany and abroad also brings a certain diversity that allows you to get to know other cultures and broaden your own perspective."
Christina Stigler - Student


"After studying business administration, I made a conscious decision to do a Master's degree in business psychology in order to find out more about people as a resource and the psychological background and motivations behind business decisions. During the degree programme, the students' interests were always taken into account in the best possible way, which is how the focus of the teaching was determined. The professionally and especially personally competent lecturers, as well as the university's good contacts with companies in the region, for example for project work, which were very important to me personally, rounded off the study experience perfectly for me."
Maximilian Karl - Student

## Practical reference

In the Master's degree programme in Applied Business Psychology, theory is brought to life immediately - through practice-oriented research projects, real company collaborations and innovative learning formats.

One particular highlight is the MindCanvas project , which was launched at the Institute of Psychology & Behavioural Science (IPBS) at OTH Amberg-Weiden. ## ADMISSION REQUIREMENTS

Would you like to apply for the Medical Engineering degree programme? To be admitted to OTH Amberg-Weiden, you need

- University entrance qualification

- General higher education entrance qualification,
- Subject-specific higher education entrance qualification or
- Technical college entrance qualification.
- Admission via vocational higher education access is also possible.
- Applicants with a school leaving certificate from a foreign school are required to submit a certificate of recognition of their school leaving certificate (VPD)*

- Language skills

Due to the unique profile of the programme, the following regulations also apply:

a. English

All applicants must also demonstrate English language skills at B2 level according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages. Ways of proving this:

- University entrance qualification in English
- University degree already obtained in English
- Abitur grade in English (German Abitur)
- Alternatively, a valid/current
- ALTE (Level 3)
- UNIcert® II
- Cambridge English (First/FCE)
- TOEFL (min. 72)
- IELTS (5.0 or better)
- PTE Academic (min. 59)
- TOEIC (min. 785)

b. German

- Additional regulations for applicants who did not obtain their university entrance qualification in German : For final enrolment, i.e. at the start of your studies , You must provide proof of German A2 !

Why is this necessary? During the first two stages of your studies, you should acquire the technical and linguistic skills necessary to enter the German labour market at the start of the practical study semester and to be able to complete the third stage of your studies partly in German, provided you choose the appropriate specialisation module. To this end, you will use Basic Electives 1-4, which are specified in more detail in the module handbook. In order to enable you to acquire these skills within the first two study sections, you must already demonstrate sufficient knowledge of the German language at the start of your studies by providing proof of language proficiency in accordance with level A2 of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages.

- Proof is not required if the university entrance qualification or a university degree has already been obtained in German.

If you have any questions about application, admissions, enrolment and semester fees, etc. , please contact Kathrin Forster .

The final decision on admission to the degree programme is made by the examination board.

*Your secondary school credentials need to be assessed here in Germany by a recognized institution (e.g UniAssist) by the end of the application period. You may apply online at the OTH before, but you will not receive a placement offer until the VPD report of your credentials is uploaded to the application portal PRIMUSS. Applicants should allow enough time for the assessment as this can take up to six weeks.

In cooperation with ARBER Seminare (https://www.arber-campus.de/masterstudium-handels-und-gesellschaftsrecht) and AK Jura (https://www.ak-jura.de/master-laws-llm) , you can directly integrate the specialist lawyer training course (Fachanwaltslehrgang) into the program. ## Job opportunities

After completing a Master’s in Trade and Corporate Law (LL.M.) , a wide range of career opportunities opens up in the legal departments of industrial, commercial, and service companies.

Graduates can take on specialist and leadership roles , for example in contract and corporate law, compliance, corporate advisory, contract management, or risk management.

Thanks to the practice-oriented training and additional qualifications such as the specialist lawyer course, they are also well prepared for responsible positions in internationally operating companies or law firms.

At OTH Amberg-Weiden, we combine sound theory with practical learning. Small groups, modern facilities, personal support and close cooperation with companies create the best study conditions.
This is also confirmed by the excellent StudyCheck ratings and the success of our graduates. Those who study here are well prepared for the future.

- Practice-oriented training: Direct relevance to tasks in legal departments of industrial, commercial, and service companies.
- International focus: Development of knowledge and competencies to succeed in an increasingly globalized professional environment.
- Professional development: Preparation for specialist and leadership roles in companies and law firms.
- Flexible study structure: An ideal combination of full-time employment and practice-oriented continuing education.
- Expert knowledge: First-hand expertise from leading academics and industry professionals.
- Networking opportunities: Direct exchange with experienced lecturers and practitioners from the field.

Continuing education credits:

The independent publication of your master’s thesis in legal journals, edited volumes, or specialist books may, under certain circumstances, be credited toward mandatory continuing education requirements pursuant to Section 15 of the German Specialist Lawyers’ Regulations (FAO). The decision on recognition lies with the respective competent bar association.

The work-study Master’s program in Trade and Corporate Law (LL.M.) is designed for working professionals who have completed a university degree, particularly lawyers holding the First or Second State Examination.

Section: Studies Study offers Study programmes

### Applied Business Informatics – Connect people, business and technology!

How can processes be made smarter? Which data drives real decisions forward? And how does technology become a success factor in a company?
In the Applied Business Informatics (AWI) programme, you will learn to combine business and IT in a practical way – with a mix of digitalisation, management and technology.

Your studies: application-oriented & individual. You will spend around 50% of your study time on practical projects , in laboratories, on case studies and on a six-month internship – closely linked to companies in the region. Our promise: you will come into contact with at least ten companies during your studies. This allows you to build up your professional network early on – and gain real insights.

Whether you prefer to broaden your horizons or specialise is up to you: you can shape your profile in the elective area – for example, with a focus on AI management, e-commerce, smart logistics or digital business consulting . Those who pursue one of these specialisations will receive a certificate in their chosen core competence in addition to their Bachelor's degree . Learning takes place in small groups, with modern technology, direct supervision and real-world challenges – hands-on, networked and future-oriented.

## Study

## Career prospects

Business informatics has been one of the most popular fields of study for years.
With a focus on applied IT and business practice, the Applied Business Informatics programme puts you in a particularly secure position for the future. Graduates are sought after across all industries – and can often choose their job .

Today, companies are constantly faced with the same questions: What does new technology offer us? What do we really need? How can we use it to create real added value?
You develop the answers – as a bridge builder between IT and business.

After completing your studies, you could work as, for example:

- Project manager for digital transformation
- Business analyst or data analyst
- Consultant for IT-related business processes
- Process or product manager for digitalisation
- E-commerce, social media or logistics expert
- Founder of a digital business model

Whether in corporations, medium-sized companies, start-ups or as a founder, your bachelor's degree qualifies you for demanding tasks.

### A career path as a business IT specialist in industry

## VERY GOOD RATINGS - VERY GOOD PROSPECTS

At OTH Amberg-Weiden, we combine sound theory with practical learning. Small groups, modern facilities, personal support and close cooperation with companies create the best study conditions. This is also confirmed by the excellent StudyCheck ratings and the success of our graduates. Those who study here are well prepared for the future.

Study-Check Ratings (https://www.studycheck.de/hochschulen/oth-aw)

## HIGHLIGHTS of the course

Practical experience, tools, teamwork – and you right in the middle of it all: Applied Business Informatics means not just learning how it works, but applying it directly. What to expect? A degree programme in which around half of the content consists of real-world practice. Whether in project seminars, case studies, laboratory units or the integrated six-month practical semester – you will work on real-world issues, often in collaboration with companies from the region.

You will become part of interdisciplinary teams , present your results to partner companies and gain valuable experience with methods from everyday professional life. You will work with modern tools – from business intelligence software and process modelling to ERP systems such as SAP.

Theory? Yes – but always application-oriented . Instead of traditional lectures, you can expect interactive teaching formats, blended learning, agile working methods and research-oriented projects in modern laboratories.

Another special feature is that AWI is not a rigid course of study. You design it yourself – with freely selectable specialisations, practical elective modules and individual project work tailored to your interests and goals. In short: at AWI, you will not only grow professionally, but also become an active part of the digital economy from the very first semester – with responsibility, freedom to act and a close connection to reality.

## Certification Programmes

In addition to your regular studies, you can take certification courses at OTH Amberg-Weiden free of charge - for example in the areas of project management or digitalisation. These additional qualifications are a real plus for your CV and help you to position yourself specifically in your professional field. You can find an overview of all certificates here:

Certifications

## Structure

In the Applied Business Informatics (B.Sc.) programme at OTH Amberg-Weiden, you will earn 210 ECTS credits in seven semesters – in an interdisciplinary, practical and flexible programme. You will start with a solid foundation in economics, computer science and digitalisation : business administration, economics, mathematics, IT systems, software fundamentals and business process modelling are just as much a part of the curriculum as digital transformation, data analysis and business intelligence.

From the third semester onwards, you will deepen your knowledge in application-oriented modules such as enterprise resource planning (ERP), process management, low-code development and business informatics projects with companies. You will use modern tools such as SAP, data visualisation systems and modelling software directly in a practical context.

What makes this programme special is that you can tailor your studies to your individual needs . From the fourth semester onwards, you will choose two of the following four specialisations:

- AI Management
- E-Commerce Management
- Smart Logistics
- Digital Business Consulting

At the same time, you will develop your soft skills – e.g. in project management, communication, self-organisation or interdisciplinary work – and train how to solve complex tasks in teams in a structured manner.

Do you want to not only study but also earn money and gain real-world work experience? Then start your dual degree program in Applied Business Informatics—and combine your studies, practical experience, and income right from the start.

At OTH Amberg-Weiden, you have two models to choose from:

Study with in-depth practical experience: You study full-time as usual and spend your lecture-free periods at a partner company. This way, you gain even more professional experience, work on real-world tasks—and build a strong career network early on. (This option is particularly popular.)

Combined study program: You combine your studies with regular vocational training—ideal if you also want to earn an IHK or HWK certification.

# German Centre for Digital Tasks in Higher Education Teaching (DZdA)

The DZdA is a nationwide initiative for the sustainable development, provision and maintenance of quality-assured, multilingual digital exercises and examination tasks. The aim is to establish a permanent infrastructure that gives all German universities access to digital tasks using the best available technology – with a focus on STACK, JSXGraph and Moodle .

The DZdA offers teachers on-demand services for creating and adapting high-quality tasks, supported by a central repository that provides didactically tested, taxonomised tasks. In addition, training courses, didactic-pedagogical advice and training programmes are being developed. The establishment of specialised centres – including for task development, didactics, AI innovation, transfer and students – is creating a nationwide teaching architecture that professionalises digital teaching and promotes individualised learning.

In the long term, the DZdA aims to become institutionalised and independent of third-party funding , and sees itself as a driving force for quality, openness and innovation in university teaching.

## Dual Degree Program in Applied Business Informatics – Your Opportunity to Recruit Highly Qualified Specialists

### Secure the skilled workers you really need—trained in real-world skills, cost-effective, and digitally competent.

In the dual degree program in Applied Business Informatics (B.Sc.) at OTH Amberg-Weiden, your future employees combine in-depth academic knowledge with practical experience gained directly within your company. Even while they are still studying, students work on concrete projects, bringing current topics from their coursework into the workplace—and vice versa. This opens up new avenues for knowledge and results transfer.

You can also be flexible in your approach: Whether the focus is on e-commerce, AI, logistics, or consulting—target the skill profile that best fits your needs.

Whether through a combined program with IHK/HWK vocational training or a degree program with in-depth practical experience—you actively shape the training and secure the right talent for your digitalization projects.

## Two models – one goal: practical training with added value

The dual degree program in Applied Business Informatics (B.Sc.) can be implemented through two proven models. Both offer your company the opportunity to develop professionals with both academic and practical qualifications—equipped with exactly the expertise you need.

### Combined degree program = Bachelor's degree program + recognized vocational training (e.g., IHK/HWK)

Your dual-track students begin with a standard apprenticeship at your company and, after approximately 12–14 months, also start their studies at OTH Amberg-Weiden.
They remain employed at your company throughout the entire training period—up to and beyond the IHK/HWK examination.

Your benefits at a glance:

- Early integration into company processes
- High proportion of practical training throughout the entire program
- Ideal for existing training structures

### Degree program with in-depth practical training = Degree program + intensive practical training phases during the program

This program emphasizes extensive practical work experience, particularly during breaks between semesters and during the internship semester. Vocational training is not included in this program—but this makes the transition to a specialist or management position after graduation particularly seamless.

Your benefits at a glance:

- High flexibility in program design
- Practical placements tailored to company needs
- Ideal for targeted professional development in specialized fields

Our goal: a win-win situation for both sides
We’ll help you choose the right model, navigate the formal process, and draft the contract. Even companies that haven’t partnered with us before can join at any time!

## Your Benefits as a Partner Company

A dual degree program in Applied Business Informatics (AWI) is more than just a training model—it is your strategic investment in the skilled professionals of tomorrow.

Here’s why a dual degree program is a worthwhile investment for your company:

- Highly qualified staff, trained to meet your specific needs—your dual students combine up-to-date academic knowledge with practical, proven skills—tailored specifically to your requirements.
- Early commitment – long-term benefits – Dual students grow into your structures from day one and develop a strong emotional connection to your company.
- Competitive advantage in the skilled labor market – Show that you prioritize training with a future – this strengthens your employer brand and attracts committed talent.
- Smooth Transition into the Workplace – Intensive practical placements eliminate long onboarding periods – your future employees are ready to work immediately.
- Flexible Training Model – Whether with or without vocational training – you choose the model that best fits your capacity and goals.

Did you know?
The retention rate for dual-track students is nearly 100%. You’re not just training them—you’re securing your future—with employees who already know you and your processes.

## How to Become a Partner Company

Would you like to nurture dual-track talent and attract them to your company early on? Partnering with OTH Amberg-Weiden is simple and flexible.

Become a partner in just a few steps:

1. Choose a study model:
Select one of the two models:

Study program with in-depth practical training – the recommended model for the AWI program
(Academic studies + intensive practical placements, no vocational training)

Combined program – a combination of academic studies and recognized vocational training (e.g., IHK)

2. Create a position within the company:
Define a suitable practical placement – e.g., in the fields of IT, digitalization, marketing, data analysis, or process management.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) from Businesses

####

In the Applied Business Informatics program, students acquire comprehensive skills in business, digitalization, and IT. Courses in areas such as process management, data analysis, software development, ERP systems, e-commerce, and AI specifically prepare them for practical tasks in the workplace. Through project work, the internship semester, and the bachelor’s thesis, your company can actively contribute to shaping the program’s academic focus.

####

The possible roles are diverse and depend on your areas of expertise and the students' interests. Typical responsibilities include:

- Collaboration on digitization or IT projects

- Support with online marketing
- Process optimization using digital tools
- Working with ERP, CRM, or e-commerce systems

####

In the “Study with In-Depth Practical Training” program, theory and practical phases alternate systematically. Students spend time at your company, particularly during breaks between semesters and during the practical training semester (6th semester). We will coordinate the exact schedule with you—flexibly and with planning certainty.

####

You pay your dual-track students during their practical training periods at the company. Many companies base their pay on the training stipends set by collective bargaining agreements (e.g., 80–100% starting in the third semester). Payment is possible but not mandatory for theoretical phases at the university. We provide personalized advice and can also provide contract templates upon request.

####

You can either actively recruit new talent on your own or rely on our support. We’ll help you connect with interested students—through college fairs, applicant pools, our Career Service team, or online platforms. Students who are already enrolled can also join a dual degree program starting in their second semester.

####

Yes—you can join at any time. We’ll work with you to determine the right program (combined study or in-depth practical training), finalize the cooperation agreement, and assist with all organizational matters. Whether you’re a large corporation or a small-to-medium-sized business, we’ll ensure our partnership is streamlined and flexible.

## Dual Degree Program in Applied Business Informatics – Your Launchpad to a Career

### Study. Earn money. Gain practical experience.

Start your dual degree program at OTH Amberg-Weiden and combine IT, business, and real-world projects in a company—with a full salary, strong career opportunities, and maximum practical experience.

Your benefits at a glance:

- Earn money from day one
- Hands-on experience directly in the company
- Up-to-date academic knowledge
- Personal guidance + teamwork
- Bachelor’s degree + professional experience in one step

## Two models – one goal: practical training with added value

In the dual degree program in Applied Business Informatics (B.Sc.), you can choose between two proven models—both of which perfectly combine theory and practice and provide targeted preparation for your future career.

### Combined degree program = Bachelor's degree program + recognized vocational training (e.g., IHK/HWK)

In the dual study program, you start with recognized vocational training at a company—for example, earning a certificate from the Chamber of Industry and Commerce (IHK) or the Chamber of Crafts (HWK). After about 12 to 14 months, you’ll also begin your studies at OTH Amberg-Weiden. Throughout this time, you’ll continue working at the company and gain valuable practical experience—all the way through to your vocational qualification and beyond.

Here’s what the dual study program offers you:

- You’ll get to know the company’s processes early on
- You’ll have a high proportion of practical training throughout your studies
- Ideal if you want to combine vocational training and academic studies

### Degree program with in-depth practical training = Degree program + intensive practical training phases during the program

This track focuses on intensive practical placements—especially during breaks between semesters and during the internship semester. Vocational training is not included, but you will regularly work within a company during your studies and gain targeted professional experience.

Here’s what the program with in-depth practical experience offers you:

- You combine your studies flexibly with hands-on work
- You work on real-world projects in your desired field
- Your transition into the workforce will be particularly seamless

Our goal: To help you get off to a successful start in your studies and career
We’ll help you find the right program for you—whether you already have a company lined up or are still looking. Even if your dream company isn’t yet a partner: A dual degree program is almost always possible!

## Why a dual degree program is worth it for you

A dual degree program in Applied Business Informatics (AWI) offers you the perfect combination of theory and practice—and opens up excellent career prospects for your professional start.

Your benefits at a glance:

- Meaningful and practical studies —you don’t just learn in lectures; you apply your knowledge directly within a company. This makes you the bridge between IT and business.
- Valuable practical experience from the start – Whether in a combined program or a program with an in-depth practical component: You’ll work on real projects, learn about business processes, and gain important professional experience – long before graduation.
- Start your career early – Thanks to the intensive practical training, you’ll be ready to hit the ground running after graduation – without a long onboarding period.
- Excellent chances of being hired – Many dual-track students stay with the company right after graduation – a nearly 100% retention rate speaks for itself.
- Earn while you study – During your practical training phases, you receive compensation – this provides you with financial security while you study.

In short:
You’ll learn through hands-on experience, build a strong professional network, receive early support—and in the end, you’ll have not only a bachelor’s degree but also real-world professional experience under your belt.

“Thanks to the combination of theory and practice, the dual degree program allowed me to figure out, step by step, what I wanted to do professionally. The support from instructors, the direct insight into the company, and the opportunity to network with colleagues early on were all incredibly helpful. The program provided me with financial security and, in the end, a permanent position. Today, I work as a Process Manager at the same company. My tip: Take advantage of the benefits of a dual degree program: real-world experience, financial security, valuable networks, and the opportunity to find your own path!”
Tobias Rupprecht - Process Manager, BHS, former BA student

# STACK Net

The STACK Net project, which has been funded by the Foundation for Innovation in Higher Education Teaching (https://stiftung-hochschullehre.de/) until March 2026 has built up a strong German-speaking community. Starting with 16 founding members, the network has grown to over 200 members (https://stack-connect.oth-aw.de/unser-team/) and now comprises four well-established core areas: the quarterly STACK Newsletter featuring contributions from the community; the networking website STACK Connect which includes an interactive map of active users; the dialogue-based STACK Talk event held in the early evening and the annual advisory board meeting .

The activities have been institutionalised and will be continued by the Service Centre for Digital Exercises at OTH Amberg-Weiden beyond the funding period.

Further information on current activities, resources and contact persons can be found on the STACK Connect - networking website.

## Information Systems & Management

The Information Systems & Management degree program prepares students to design, manage, and use information systems to support organizational goals and decision-making. The program combines business management principles with information technology, focusing on systems analysis, data management, cybersecurity, and enterprise systems. Graduates gain the skills needed to bridge the gap between technical teams and management, ensuring effective, secure, and efficient use of information systems in modern organizations.

## Job opportunities

Globalization, digitalization, and social change demand modern leadership, new structures, and advanced technologies. A Master’s in Information Systems & Management prepares graduates for these challenges by combining IT expertise with business and management skills. This unique profile opens diverse career paths such as IT Project Management, Business Analysis, Consulting , and Digital Transformation across multiple industries.

Beyond technical knowledge, the program develops leadership, strategic, and analytical skills. Graduates benefit from high flexibility, and excellent long-term career prospects in an increasingly data-driven and digital world, ready to take responsibility for projects, teams, and complex digital initiatives. This Master’s program provides a future-proof foundation for long-term professional success in global corporations, medium-sized enterprises, and start-ups alike.

## VERY GOOD RATINGS - VERY GOOD PROSPECTS

At OTH Amberg-Weiden , the Master’s program Information Systems & Management builds on a long-standing tradition of excellence across a wide range of closely connected disciplines or faculties. Our program brings together expertise from technology, business, and management to deliver an interdisciplinary learning experience that truly reflects real-world practice.

We combine solid academic theory with hands-on, practical learning. Small class sizes, state-of-the-art facilities, personalized support, and close cooperation with industry partners create an outstanding learning environment and ideal study conditions. Our quality is reflected in excellent StudyCheck ratings and, most importantly, in the professional success of our graduates.

Study-Check Ratings (https://www.studycheck.de/hochschulen/oth-aw)

## HIGHLIGHTS of the course

- International Orientation meets Interdisciplinary Focus
English-taught curriculum that combines information technology, business administration, and management taught in a multicultural study environment to prepare students for leadership roles in the digital global economy
- Practice-Oriented Learning in Small Class Sizes
Strong emphasis on real-world projects and case studies in an interactive learning environment with personal support and direct access to professors
- Excellent Career Prospects with a Future-Oriented Curriculum
Graduates are highly sought after in roles such as IT management, consulting, business analysis, and digital transformation in regionally rooted small or mid-sized companies as well as large global players

## Structure

The Master’s programme Information Systems & Management is structured as a 5-semester advanced training degree programme with a total of 90 ECTS . The curriculum is organized into mandatory modules, elective modules, and the final thesis phase.

### BUSINESS INNOVATION & ENTREPRENEURSHIP – Make more of ideas & ventures

You’re in the middle of your career, want to take on more responsibility and further your professional development—but you certainly don’t want to give up everything else to do so. Or have you just completed your bachelor’s degree and want to learn how to become an entrepreneur, whether in a traditional job, a startup, or by launching your own business? That’s exactly why we developed the Master’s program in “Business Innovation and Entrepreneurship.”

Thanks to the modern hybrid study model —which combines online instruction, compact on-campus sessions (typically about two days a week) at the Kemnath Campus, and select intensive courses—the program is easily compatible with work, family, and daily life. In addition, the Business Innovation & Entrepreneurship program offers students the unique opportunity to actively help shape the curriculum. Small cohorts foster close interaction and enable the creation of a learning environment tailored to the demands of modern businesses and the needs of students.

The program focuses on modern management skills, innovation, entrepreneurship, and intrapreneurship . It’s not just about starting your own business. It’s about recognizing opportunities, taking responsibility, and actively shaping change. Not every graduate will start a business. But every graduate will learn to think and act like an entrepreneur.

## Career prospects

With your Master’s in Business Innovation and Entrepreneurship (M.A.), you’ll have a modern skill set : entrepreneurial thinking, innovation methods, strategic analysis skills, leadership competencies, and technological openness.

Typical career paths include:

- Project Lead
- Innovation Manager / Intrapreneur
- Business Development Manager
- Product Manager
- Digital Strategy Manager
- Strategic Management Consulting
- Founder / Co-Founder of your own company
- Employee at a startup
- Roles in accelerators, incubators, or venture capital environments
- Public Sector Innovation & Social Entrepreneurship
- Advanced academic qualification (Ph.D.)

The Master’s program qualifies you for both leadership roles with significant responsibility and independent entrepreneurial activities .

## VERY GOOD RATINGS - VERY GOOD PROSPECTS

At OTH Amberg-Weiden, we combine sound theory with practical learning. Small groups, modern facilities, personal support and close cooperation with companies create the best study conditions. This is also confirmed by the excellent StudyCheck ratings and the success of our graduates. Those who study here are well prepared for the future.

Study-Check Ratings (https://www.studycheck.de/hochschulen/oth-aw)

## HIGHLIGHTS of the course

Real Projects. Real Impact. Mastering Innovation.

In the Master’s program in Business Innovation and Entrepreneurship, you’ll develop innovation not in the classroom—but in the real world . Entrepreneurial action is always at the heart of the program—whether in a startup, a small-to-medium-sized business, or a DAX-listed company. What that means: hands-on, interdisciplinary, and always results-oriented.

What you can look forward to:

- Applied teaching to solve real-world challenges
- Modern management skills, particularly strategic, process-oriented, and psychological competencies
- Methodological training and the use of practical “tools” for everyday business operations
- Maximum student involvement for extensive hands-on experience and “learning by doing”
- Projects and assignments from regional companies ensure practical relevance and offer maximum networking opportunities
- Case studies (regional, national, international) to illustrate the course content
- Theory? Yes, but kept concise and with a clear focus: guidance for solving business problems

Look forward to a learning environment that is second to none. The new Kemnath Campus is currently being built from the ground up. That means: state-of-the-art facilities, plenty of open space, and ample opportunity to get involved. The new Kemnath Campus is thus more than just a place of study—it is a space for entrepreneurial possibilities . This is where ideas and teams are born, and where the skills and management talents of tomorrow grow.

## Structure

In the Master's program in Business Innovation and Entrepreneurship, you will deepen your knowledge of innovation, entrepreneurship and strategic management. The Master's programme combines scientific foundations with a consistent practical orientation and provides you with a clear content profile in the following areas:

- Innovation & Business Transformation
- Start-up & Corporate Entrepreneurship
- Entrepreneurial Finance & Investment
- Leadership & Change Management

Project-based teaching formats, interactive seminars and real-world innovation projects promote analytical thinking and entrepreneurial implementation skills. You will work systematically with scientific methods and develop the ability to translate complex economic issues into viable business models. Courses are usually taught in clusters. This compact structure creates space for intensive project work, exchange in the innovation environment and the independent development of start-up and innovation projects.

You will be accompanied by experienced professors and practical experts from the innovation and start-up environment. Personal support in small, international cohorts enables intensive exchange and individual feedback. At the Kemnath study location, you will benefit from an innovative learning environment in a rural area with close links between science, business and regional development .

# Application Information (M.A. Business Innovation and Entrepreneurship)

## Access and admission requirements

You can apply for a spot in the program during the application period via the OTH Amberg-Weiden application portal. General information on the application, admission, and enrollment process can be found here:

To be admitted to the Master’s program in Business Innovation and Entrepreneurship , you must have:

- A successfully completed bachelor’s degree or equivalent university degree with 210 ECTS credits (at least 180 ECTS credits).
- Generally, a final grade of “good” or better. Alternatively, program-specific aptitude can be demonstrated through an aptitude test.
- English proficiency at a minimum of B2 level (CEFR).
- German proficiency at a minimum of B2 level (CEFR).
- A degree in a relevant field. This includes, in particular, programs in economics, interdisciplinary fields, and technology-oriented disciplines. The admissions committee determines the relevance of the degree.
- If you have a bachelor’s degree worth 180 ECTS credits, any missing credits can be made up during the program.
- If you have not yet completed your bachelor’s degree at the time of application, you may apply under certain conditions and submit the required documentation later.

Detailed regulations can be found in § 5 of the program’s Study and Examination Regulations .

## FAQs

Here you'll find frequently asked questions about our “Business Innovation and Entrepreneurship” program.

Note: You can search for keywords using Ctrl + F (Windows) or Command + F (Mac).

### Questions concerning the study course

####

## Is this a new study program?

Yes. And it’s truly new.

Business Innovation & Entrepreneurship has been developed entirely from scratch—not as a revamp of an existing program, but built from the ground up with a clear goal: to help people take on responsibility, recognize opportunities, and actively drive things forward. It’s explicitly not just about starting your own business. The program is equally aimed at anyone who wants to take on responsibility in existing companies, shape innovation, or develop their leadership skills.

In short: If you want to do more than just work—if you want to help shape the future—you’ve come to the right place.

####

## Let's be honest: Why should I choose this master's program?

Because we don’t offer just any old master’s program here. Business Innovation and Entrepreneurship is a high-quality, exciting, and diverse program. It focuses entirely on modern management skills, strategic and process-oriented methods, agile workflows, and—most importantly—key personal skills that build on your individual strengths. On top of that, you’ll work with modern tools, analyze numerous case studies, and engage in plenty of hands-on applications. One thing’s for sure: you won’t get bored.

####

## What is the course about?

It’s about entrepreneurship and intrapreneurship—that is, entrepreneurial thinking and action in the workplace, no matter where that may be. We emphasize training in the latest methods, the use of practical tools, and lots and lots of case studies.

####

## Theory or practice?

Definitely practice. We’ll focus 100% on hands-on work, try out lots of different things, collaborate with real companies, and won’t have any exams.

####

## How exactly? No exams?

Exactly! No exams.

####

## What are my possibilities after the course?

Everything you need to know as a manager, project manager, team leader, entrepreneur, or business founder. Everything. I promise.

####

## Can I study for the master's degree while working?

Yes, definitely—that’s exactly what we want to achieve. We also want you to gain further qualifications while continuing to work in your current positions. That’s why we’ll be using a hybrid model: remote on Mondays, and in Kemnath on Tuesdays and Wednesday mornings.

####

## How much time does it take each week?

Of course, a master’s program requires time and dedication. Students earn 30 ECTS credits per semester. At the same time, we have deliberately designed the program to be as compatible as possible with a full-time job. Many courses are held online, some are offered in intensive blocks, and part of the learning can be scheduled flexibly. Of course, the actual time commitment depends on individual prior knowledge, learning pace, and personal expectations. However, our goal is to offer a program that can be integrated into everyday professional life in a practical and realistic way and, above all, is and remains feasible alongside a full-time job.

####

## What if I can't manage to balance my studies with my job?

Thanks to the small class sizes and close collaboration between faculty and students, we are able to address individual challenges and opportunities on a highly personalized basis. There is certainly a solution for every problem.

####

## What makes this program special?

It’s new, it’s breaking new ground, it’s located at the brand-new Kemnath Campus, and it will continue to evolve in an agile way together with you. As students, you’ll contribute to this and help shape its future. And yes, the faculty has an entrepreneurial spirit in their blood.

####

## Will I have to start a business later on?

No. Entrepreneurship is an important part of the program, but by no means its sole objective. The program is equally aimed at people who wish to take on responsibility within companies, drive innovation, or assume leadership roles.

####

## Is there a tuition fee?

(POC: Susanne Winterl )
This program does not require tuition payment by neither national nor international students. There is no tuition fee, but you have to pay 87€ per semester for administrative matters (student identity card etc.) as well as 500€ service fee for each semester. If you want to apply for the program, you have to pay 50€ for your application before you can send your application in the Primuss Portal.
Learn more…

### Questions concerning your study location

####

## Where is the program held?

Mainly on site in Kemnath, at the brand-new facilities of the OTH Amberg-Weiden’s Kemnath Campus.

####

## Why Kemnath?

It’s simple: Kemnath has much more to offer than many people realize at first glance. The new Kemnath Campus is creating a modern learning environment with short distances, a personal atmosphere, and close interaction between students and faculty. Added to this is an exciting environment with successful companies in the region, including Siemens Healthineers, Ponnath, and IGZ. We also benefit from an active entrepreneurial and startup network, the Technology Transfer Center (TTZ), and Co-Working Kemnath. Support from local and regional policymakers further creates ideal conditions for new ideas, projects, and collaborations.

And honestly: For a degree program focused on innovation, entrepreneurship, and future-oriented topics, we can hardly imagine a more suitable environment.

####

## How to get to Kemnath?

All students will be able to come to campus—we promise.

- By car: The Kemnath campus is easily accessible by car—there is plenty of parking available right on campus.
- By train: Kemnath also has a train station. We will set up a shuttle service from the station to the campus to transport every student from the station to the campus (travel time approx. 5 minutes).
- With SpaceX: Immediately after the IPO, our program director will contact Elon Musk.

####

## Are there accessible entrances?

Yes there are accessible entrances.

### Questions about studying in Germany

####

## Where can I find a room or a place to stay in Kemnath, or who should I contact?

If you'd like to live in Kemnath, you can ask us for a list of housing options.

####

## As a foreigner, am I allowed to work in Germany while I am here on a student visa?

Yes, you can work up to 20 hours a week.

####

## Do I need German health insurance when I start my studies at OTH Amberg-Weiden?

(POC: Andreas Schaller)
Yes. Please contact our health insurance specialist, Mr. Schaller, at Techniker Krankenkasse. He will help you sign up for health insurance. You can also do this online. If you would like a comprehensive package through TK’s partner, Expatrio, follow this link: www.expatrio.com (https://www.expatrio.com/) .

In this context, ‘practical’ does not mean simply carrying out predefined tasks for companies, but taking on entrepreneurial responsibility . You develop your own ideas, test assumptions under real-world market conditions, and make decisions that impact business models, resources and growth.

During your studies, you work interactively : hypotheses are tested, concepts adapted and solutions refined – often with direct feedback from the start-up and innovation community. Instead of simulations, real projects emerge that can be continued, financed or launched.

In doing so, you combine scientific methods with entrepreneurial action . You learn to structure uncertainty, systematically evaluate opportunities and not only plan innovation, but also implement it. This fosters a practical understanding that prepares you for roles requiring creativity, responsibility and initiative.

## Networks for your future

Innovation rarely happens in isolation. That is why the degree programme is closely integrated into an active innovation and start-up network that supports you throughout your studies and provides you with real-world access to practical experience, funding and collaboration opportunities. You won’t be working on ideas in isolation, but will engage with founders, companies, funding bodies and partner organisations – building contacts early on that will continue to benefit you long after you’ve graduated.

This network is supported by key partners and venues that actively facilitate innovation and start-ups in Kemnath , the programme’s location.

# Office for Research and Transfer

## Research and Transfer Office

#### Supporting the journey from funding concept to societal impact

The Office for Research and Transfer is the central hub for research, technology and knowledge transfer, and science communication at OTH Amberg-Weiden. We support researchers, professors, and early-career academics in the planning, application, and implementation of research and transfer projects. Acting as a university-wide interface, the office connects academia, business, industry, and society.
We provide advice on funding programs and external grants, assist with research proposals, and enhance the visibility of research conducted at OTH Amberg-Weiden. Furthermore, we offer support regarding science communication, collaborations, and knowledge transfer activities. We also coordinate doctoral studies at our university.
Our goal is to create optimal conditions for successful research and to foster innovative projects in a sustainable manner.

[Image: Team des Instituts für Angewandte Forschung (IAF) der OTH Amberg-Weiden] Hanna Gallitzendörfer (Innovative Learning Spaces), Veronika Wiesmet (Officer for R&D and Transfer), Markus Ringer (Managing Director of the Doctoral Center), Andrea Breitschaft (Assistant), Bernhard Gschrey (University Development), Nicole Karzmarczyk (Assistant), Michael Tschapka (Officer for R&D and Transfer), Wolfgang Weber (Vice President for R&D and Transfer), and Maria Pusoma (Science Communication).

## Our key areas of activity

### Research

#### Third-party funding, framework conditions, early-career researchers

We take care of the framework – you focus on the research.

We support professors and early-career researchers in the development, planning, and implementation of research projects:

- Advice on aligning individual research with the university’s research profile
- Assistance in identifying suitable funding programs—ranging from regional to international levels
- Guidance on grant applications and the strategic orientation of research projects and doctoral procedures
- Commitment to improving the framework conditions for research
- Advice on doctoral opportunities and cooperative doctoral models at OTH Amberg-Weiden

### Communication

#### Visibility of research for mutual transfer

Making research visible, accessible and relatable.

We support researchers in communicating their projects, results, and impact in a way that is clear, targeted, and compliant with funding requirements:

- Strategic planning of institutional research communication and external science communication
- Advice on science communication and the presentation of impact in grant proposals
- Support in selecting suitable communication formats for diverse target audiences
- Operational assistance with implementation, e.g., for website content and social media formats

Our focus is on authentic communication that remains close to the science and makes research visible.

### Technology transfer

#### Putting research into exchange and application

Share knowledge and thus shape innovation together.

We foster exchange between academia, industry, policymakers, and society, creating spaces for knowledge transfer and networking:

- Publications and information channels such as newsletters, research reports, and social media
- Internal event formats, e.g., research forums or workshops on key current topics
- Knowledge transfer activities and networking initiatives with external partners
- Support for external events such as academic congresses, conferences, and outreach programs
- Use of transfer and technology centers as hubs for exchange and practical application

# System-Check

The ‘System Check’ is a requirement set out in the 2023–2027 Higher Education Agreement (https://www.stmwk.bayern.de/download/22334_OTH-Amberg-Weiden.pdf) between OTH Amberg-Weiden and the Bavarian State Ministry of Science and Arts. It supports the systematic further development of the university’s quality assurance and quality management system. The ‘System Check’ comprises a comprehensive self-evaluation in which all processes and areas (research, teaching and administration) are examined and existing strengths as well as potential areas for improvement are identified. The results help the university management to steer internal processes and set strategic priorities, thereby contributing to the development of the university’s profile.

title: [Translate to Englisch:] Labor Biophysik der Fakultät Wirtschaftsingenieurwesen und Gesundheit (1/2)
content:
[Translate to Englisch:] Labor Biophysik der Fakultät Wirtschaftsingenieurwesen und Gesundheit
Section: Research Research environment Laboratories

## Introducing the "Biomechanics and Sports Science" Laboratory

The Laboratory for Biomechanics and Sports Science is one of the research laboratories at the Institute of Medical Technology at the East Bavarian University of Applied Sciences Amberg-Weiden. It brings together research, teaching, and industry in the field of medical technology. Research areas include gait and running analysis, spiro(ergo)metry, endoprosthetics, force measurements, and numerical simulation with a focus on multi-body simulation and the finite element method.

In partnership with HOHPE GmbH, we offer performance testing for amateur and professional athletes, among others. For more information, please visit the following link:

PERFORMANCE DIAGNOSTICS

### Teaching & Research

Gait and Posture Analysis

The Laboratory for Biomechanics and Sports Sciences is equipped with a marker-based 3D gait analysis system from Vicon (Yarnton, Oxford, UK). With a sampling rate of up to 2 MHz, 18 high-speed cameras capture the position data of body segments with an accuracy of less than 1 mm. In addition, two synchronized video reference cameras are used for 3D registration of the motion data.

The Smartsuit Pro (Rokoko, Copenhagen, Denmark) offers a mobile solution for gait analysis. Its 19 built-in inertial sensors (Inertial Measurement Units – IMUs) measure the body’s motion data.

Alternatively, gait and posture analyses can be performed almost anywhere using the EIDOO mobile 2D recording system. The 2D analysis is primarily used for routine gait assessments. In these cases, the measurement accuracy is sufficient to detect simple gait abnormalities, such as walking on tiptoes in children.

Treadmill

The Laboratory for Biomechanics and Sports Science has an approximately 18-meter-long test track available for gait and running analyses. Depending on the experimental setup, the h/p/cosmos pulsar 3P med treadmill (zebris Medical GmbH, Isny, Germany & h/p/cosmos sports & medical GmbH, Nußdorf, Germany) can also be used for gait and running analyses. To ensure safe use in performance diagnostics and for patients, the medical treadmill is equipped with a safety bar, a fall-stop system with a chest strap, and two side handrails.

Technical specifications of the treadmill:

- Running surface: 190 cm x 65 cm
- Speed: 0–40 km/h
- Incline: +/-25%
- With direction reversal
-
Built-in pressure sensor

Visual Gait Guidance

The treadmill in the Laboratory of Biomechanics and Sports Sciences is equipped with a visual gait guidance system. This system is primarily used in neurological, orthopedic, and geriatric rehabilitation. The subject’s or patient’s gait pattern is automatically recorded. This gait pattern is adjusted according to specific targets (e.g., stride length, step width, and foot angle). The gait pattern is projected onto the treadmill, and the subject. The gait pattern is projected onto the treadmill, and the subject tries to follow it. This can help correct gait abnormalities and improve gait symmetry.

Pedobarography

Pedobarography refers to the static or dynamic analysis of pressure distribution on the sole of the foot during various activities of daily living. The Laboratory of Biomechanics and Sports Sciences offers two different instrumental methods. First, pressure sensors with a sensing area of 162.6 cm x 54.2 cm (12,288 sensors & sampling rate: 100 Hz) are integrated into the treadmill deck. In addition, OpenGo sensor insoles (Moticon ReGo AG, Munich, Germany) in sizes 36–47 are used to measure pressure distribution inside the shoe.

Force plates

Force plates are used to determine the kinetics of the human body. In biomechanics, they are used, among other things, to measure ground reaction forces when the foot strikes the ground during walking and to perform jump analyses. The Laboratory of Biomechanics and Sports Sciences is equipped with two force plates from Bertec (Columbus, Ohio, USA) and two portable force plates (Kistler Instruments AG, Winterthur, Switzerland) with a surface area of 60 cm x 60 cm. The results of gait analysis and kinetics are used, for example, to plan therapeutic concepts, rehabilitation measures, or for multi-body simulation.

Segmentation

Cross-sectional imaging techniques such as computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) are frequently used in medicine for diagnosis and surgical planning. These images can be used to develop 3D models of anatomical structures. For example, complex bone fractures can be visualized. In addition, length measurements using this planning software—such as femoral offset—facilitate the planning of hip replacement surgery. Depending on the research question, the segmented structures—such as bones or muscles—can be reused for multi-body simulations or the finite element method, or 3D-printed for visualization.

Numerical Simulation: Finite Element Method

The finite element method (FEM) is a technique used in structural mechanics to analyze stresses and strains in bones or implants in response to applied forces. At OTH Amberg-Weiden, the simulation software ANSYS Workbench and Discovery (Canonsburg, Pennsylvania, USA) is used.

Numerical Simulation: Multibody Simulation

Multibody simulation is used to calculate joint reaction forces and muscle forces in the body. A multi-body simulation model typically consists of bones, joints, and muscles. If kinematic data (e.g., via motion capture) and kinetic data (e.g., via force plates) are also incorporated, the biomechanics simulation software OpenSim (Stanford, California, USA) calculates the forces and moments that occur in the muscles and joints during movement.

Electromyography (EMG)

title: [Translate to Englisch:] Labor Biophysik der Fakultät Wirtschaftsingenieurwesen und Gesundheit (2/2)
content:
[Translate to Englisch:] Labor Biophysik der Fakultät Wirtschaftsingenieurwesen und Gesundheit
Section: Research Research environment Laboratories

Electromyography is a technical method used to measure electrical activity during muscle contraction. In clinical practice, EMG is used to diagnose neuromuscular disorders. In biomechanics, EMG sensors are used to simultaneously record the activity of various muscles during the individual phases of gait for gait analysis. Software is used to analyze both the duration and intensity of the signals. The Laboratory of Biomechanics and Sports Sciences is equipped for this purpose with a surface EMG system featuring 2 Trigno IM and 14 Trigno Avanti sensors from DELSYS INCORPORATED (Natick, Massachusetts, USA).

Spirometry, spiroergometry, lactate measurement, and electrocardiography (ECG)

Spirometry is a procedure used to diagnose a person’s lung function. Measurable parameters such as the Tiffenau index and vital capacity are used to differentiate between obstructive (e.g., bronchial asthma) and restrictive lung diseases (e.g., pulmonary fibrosis). In addition to the stationary spirometry unit, the Laboratory of Biomechanics and Sports Sciences also has a portable spirometry device (COSMED Srl, Albano Laziale, Italy).

Spiroergometry is used to examine the cardiovascular system, lung function, and energy metabolism during exercise. During spiroergometry, respiratory gases are measured and the subject’s cardiac status is monitored during exercise. The Laboratory of Biomechanics and Sports Sciences is equipped with a treadmill, an ergometer bicycle, and a mobile 12-lead ECG. In performance diagnostics, lactate levels are also used to develop optimal training plans for athletes.

Isometric and Isokinetic Force Measurement

Force measurement is crucial in sports as well as in multi-body simulation. To this end, the Laboratory for Biomechanics and Sports Sciences is equipped with an IsoMed 2000 (D. & R. Ferstl GmbH, Hemau, Germany). This device is used for performance diagnostics and training in both sports and scientific applications. Training goals are set for the test subjects, and examination protocols are created.

Single-joint training sessions are designed for the knee, shoulder, ankle, trunk, and back. For multi-joint training sessions, the horizontal leg press is available. Depending on the study or training design, movements can be performed concentrically, eccentrically, or isometrically.
